## 2b(C) THE BITMAP / BLOCK-ALLOCATION DESIGN STORY

### C.1 Geometry, all pinned by instructions

`BPB = BSIZE*8 = 8192`; `BBLOCK(b,sb) = b/BPB + sb.bmapstart`.  Offsets are
read off the tracked image (`sb.size` at `sb+4` from balloc +0x0a;
`sb.bmapstart` at `sb+28` from balloc +0xa0 / bfree +0x12; `BPB = 2^13` from
the `sraiw`/`srliw` by 0xd; `BSIZE = 1024` from the inlined bzero's `li
a2,1024`).  `bmapstart` and `size` ride as plain fractional cells — **still no
superblock abstraction**.

**`FSSIZE = 2000 < BPB = 8192`, so there is exactly ONE bitmap block.**
`0 < size ≤ BPB` is a premise of every contract here, `BBLOCK` collapses, and
balloc's outer loop runs a single iteration; only the inner bit scan is a real
loop.  `bzero` is `static` with one caller, so gcc INLINED it — there is no
`bzero` symbol.

### C.2 `BitmapEnc.v` — the encoding discipline

The third vocabulary of its kind after `BlockWords`' words and `DinodeEnc`'s
records, and it keeps the same discipline: **the block content is always in
the IMAGE of an encoding over a pure index set, so an update is a set
operation and the byte level is only ever read back.**  `bm_byte u j`,
`bm_bytes n u`, where `u` is the set of SET bits and in xv6 a set bit means IN
USE.  The arithmetic is stated on `Z` at a BIT INDEX (not a `(byte,bit)`
pair), because the code computes the byte as `bi/8` and the mask as
`1 << (bi%8)` and the 64-bit `and`/`or`/`xori -1` land exactly on
`Z.land`/`Z.lor`/`Z.lnot`.  `bm_bytes_upd`/`_set`/`_clear` are what relate a
`log_write` of the whole bitmap block to a one-element set operation.
The file is iris-free and Sail-free.

### C.3 The free-block ghost state: a POOL, not a token

```coq
pool_elt Γ u b   := if b ∈ u then emp else ∃ bs, blk_owned Γ b bs
free_pool Γ nb u := [∗ list] b ∈ seqZ 0 nb, pool_elt Γ u b
free_bitmap_at Γ bms nb u := blk_owned Γ bms (bm_bytes BSIZE u) ∗ free_pool Γ nb u
bitmap_res γfs bmapstart size used := free_bitmap_at (fs_gamma_L γfs) bmapstart size used
free_blk γfs b := ∃ bs, fsblock (fs_bytes γfs) b bs
```

Two things and no more: **the bitmap block at the IMAGE of the pure set
`used`, and — for every block below `size` whose bit reads CLEAR — that block
itself**, at content nobody has committed to.

> **Exclusivity of the byte run is the whole handshake.**  There is no
> per-block ownership token — `FsBlocks.blk_own` is gone.  It existed because
> the client resource used to be the block-keyed HALF `fs_chalf`, and two
> halves at one key are consistent, so no amount of `fs_chalf` reasoning said
> a block was unowned.  The byte view is EXCLUSIVE, so one fact does both jobs.

The two jobs:

* **balloc's freshness ⟹ injectivity.**  A caller holding one run per block
  its own structures name concludes the new block is none of them
  (`FsBlocks.fsblock_ne`, one line of the `↦`-distinctness idiom), which
  re-establishes `InodeInv.blkmap_wf`'s injectivity.  `InodeInv.inode_fresh`
  is that fact lifted to a whole block map.
* **bfree's `panic("freeing free block")` is DEAD, refuted not proved.**  The
  caller arrives holding the block's run; if the bit were CLEAR the pool would
  hold a SECOND run at that block, and two owners of one block's bytes is
  `False` (`free_pool_used` off `phi_excl`).

**`bitmap_ok` is DERIVED, not maintained.**
`bitmap_ok cov logstart size used := ∀ x, 0 ≤ x < size → x ∉ used → x ∈ cov ∧
x ∉ log_region_set logstart` is what turns "balloc found a zero bit" into the
two facts `bread` and `log_write` demand — but it is **not a conjunct of
`bitmap_res` and nothing preserves it**.  It is read off the pool's OWNERSHIP
at each `bitmap_read`, because **holding a run IS being a home block**
(`fsblock_home` against `bytes_dom`).  That is fs-state §0's "a consequence of
the `∗`" in place of a maintained clause — and it is why boot owes nothing.

### C.4 Who owns `bitmap_res` between calls

**Nobody outside `BitmapInv.v`.**  It is exclusive and there is one per file
system, so threading it through contracts serialized every allocator and freer
(and, because `fileclose`'s environment rode in the trap residue, would have
serialized user mode across all harts).  It lives in an Iris invariant at an
EXISTENTIAL set:

```coq
bitmap_body γfs bms size := ∃ used, bitmap_res γfs bms size used
bitmap_inv  γfs bms cov ls size := inv bitmapN (bitmap_body …) ∗ fs_bytes_inv …
```

Persistent; a conjunct of `FsReady.fs_ready`.  **No contract names `used`** —
balloc/bfree/bmap/writei/itrunc/iput/dirlink/create/the `sys_*` family/kexec/
fileclose/kexit/syscall/fsinit/ireclaim all take the persistent row and return
nothing about the bitmap.  "The shape is `InodeRegion`'s, one layer over": the
parked run never leaves the invariant except at `log_write`'s own ghost step.

Four lemmas are the whole interface:

| lemma | when | what |
|---|---|---|
| `bitmap_read` | between `bread` and `brelse` | the handle's machinery half against the parked run ⟹ `∃ used, bsl = bitmap_bytes used ∧ bitmap_ok … used`. Mask-preserving. |
| `bitmap_read_own` | bfree, same window | `bitmap_read` + the caller's `fsblock … b bs` ⟹ `b ∈ used` — the panic refutation. |
| `bitmap_alloc_au` | balloc's `log_write` of the bitmap block | premises `bi ∉ u0`, `0 ≤ bi < size`, `size ≤ BPB`; the wand takes the run back at `bitmap_bytes (u0 ∪ {[bi]})` and pays out `free_blk γfs bi` — **the block's byte run, AND NOTHING ELSE**. |
| `bitmap_free_au` | bfree's `log_write` | takes `free_blk γfs b` up front; re-parks at `bitmap_bytes (u0 ∖ {[b]})` and pays `emp`. Takes NO covered-ness premise. |

**The two sets need not agree**, and the suppliers are stated at the CALLER's:
at its `bread` the caller learned `bsl = bitmap_bytes u0`; by its `log_write`
the invariant parks some `u1` with `bitmap_bytes u1 = bsl` — the machinery
half froze the BYTES, not the set (bits ≥ `BPB` are invisible to the block).
`bitmap_bytes_eq_bit` transfers the one bit tested; `_ext`/`_eq_union`/
`_eq_diff` transfer the written image.  **Do not add a `used ⊆ [0,BPB)` clause
to get injectivity** — not needed, and one more thing boot would have to
establish.

### C.5 What balloc and bfree consume and produce

**`balloc`** (262 B, sleeps).  Pre: the two superblock cells at any dfracs,
`bitmap_inv`, `0 < size ≤ BPB`, `0 ≤ bmapstart`, `bmapstart ∈ cov`,
`bmapstart ∉ log_region_set logstart`; `bslots bn 2` (bread + `log_write`'s
bpin, twice, non-overlapping); budget `log_op (2+u)` in; `K_balloc = 50`.
Two arms:

* **success** — `b ≠ 0` with `⌜b ∈ cov⌝`, `⌜b ∉ log_region⌝`,
  `fsblock γfs b (replicate BSIZE 0)`: bzero has already logged the block as
  all-zero, so the caller receives a **zeroed** block.  Spends two budget
  units.  **The RUN ITSELF is the freshness claim** — without it the caller
  cannot show the block differs from one it already owns.
* **failure** — returns 0, spends nothing, gives nothing; `2+u` refunded.

`0 < size` is load-bearing twice over: it makes the single-bitmap-block
simplification sound, and it kills balloc's own `beqz a5` arm at +0x12 (which
is otherwise a live path with no s2–s8 restore).

**`bfree`** (108 B, straight line).  Consumes `fsblock γfs b bs` — **the
block's whole run and nothing beside it** — plus `bitmap_inv`; the block goes
back into the pool at its `log_write`, and **nothing about the bitmap comes
out**.  `K_bfree = 44`, `bslots bn 2`, budget **spend-exactly**
`log_op (S u) → log_op u` (bfree is straight-line and always runs its one
`log_write`, so it needs none of bmap's spend-at-most weakening).  It does NOT
read `sb.size`.

**The caller-side bundle** is `bm_alloc` / `bm_alloc_res`: the two cells, the
geometry (`bitmap_geom_ok` as a `⌜⌝`), and balloc's printk gname as ONE record
and ONE `iProp` — one binder and one resource rather than five of each, and
everything in it is pure, a returned fraction, or persistent, so it is
invariant across the whole call and no loop invariant mentions the bitmap's
state.  `bm_kit None = emp` keeps `BMAP_NOALLOC` free of it.

**The honesty caveat.**  balloc's out-of-blocks arm reaches `printk`, whose
contract is carried as a **`Prop` hypothesis** (`printk_gen_contract`), not a
functor argument — `wp_printk_gen_sconf_body` has Coq-arrow premises so it is
not an `iProp` and cannot be boxed.  This keeps balloc/bmap/writei at the
standing six axioms and pushes the obligation to whoever discharges it.  "Do
not read those six as 'depends on nothing else'."

## 2b(D) THE FS-STATE / ABSTRACTION LAYER

### D.1 The guiding rule: LOCAL reasoning (fs-state §0)

> Every spec in this design must let a proof about one inode, one directory or
> one block be done **without bringing the whole file system into the proof
> context**.

Concretely, and all four are enforced by deletion of ~15 kLOC:

* **No predicate above `inode_owned` states a pure fact about more than one
  inode.**  Whole-state pure predicates (`fs_durable_wf`, `fsimg_wf` sweeps,
  "every used block belongs to exactly one inode", "nlink equals the number of
  entries") DO NOT EXIST.  Where such a fact is needed it is a consequence of
  ownership (the `∗`) or of an RA's own law, never a maintained clause.
* **Disjointness is never stated.**  The one exclusivity law ever invoked is
  `own x ∗ own x ⊢ False`, used as `l ↦ _ ∗ l ↦ _ ⊢ False` is used — to learn
  that two owned things are different objects, never as an invariant.
* **There is no "tree".**  The abstraction is a SET of inodes, some of which
  decode as directories.
* **The log knows nothing about the file system.**  It exposes bytes and two
  logically-atomic linearization points.

### D.2 The view record `Γ`, and TWO instances of one predicate

```
Γ := { Φ : Z → bv 8 → iProp ; γlink : gname ; γtop : gname }
```

The same definitions are instantiated twice:

* **`Γ_D`, the committed (durable) view** — `Φ_D a v := a ↪[γD] v`.  Its three
  gnames are EXISTENTIAL, inside the snapshot `FsDurSnap.fs_snap Γ g D S`;
  `P_dur D` closes all of them, which is what makes the durable half of
  `FsCrash.P_fs` a function of `D` alone and lets a commit DROP one epoch and
  allocate the next.  **No mortal ever holds a piece of it.**
* **`Γ_L`, the logged (in-era) view** — `Φ_L a v := a ↪[fs_L] v`, the FULL
  element of the era's byte-keyed logged view whose auth the log owns.
  `γlink_L`/`γtop_L` are era-minted and die with the era — correct, because
  uncommitted writes must vanish at a crash.

**Bytes, not blocks, on both sides**, so an inode record can own ITS 64 bytes
of an inode block.  Ownership is EXCLUSIVE (full elements) — which is what
lets `free_bitmap`'s argument run and why bio's agreement share moved to a
bio-side map.

### D.3 The nested predicates

```
fs_state   Γ dq S  := sb_owned ∗ fs_inodes ∗ free_bitmap ∗ ⌜fs_geom S⌝   (at gamma_q Γ dq)
fs_inodes  Γ I     := [∗ map] i ↦ n ∈ I, inode_owned Γ i n     (* the one ∗-iteration *)
inode_owned Γ i n  := rec_owned Γ i n.rec
                    ∗ [∗ k ∈ slots n] blk_owned Γ (addr n k) (blocks n k)
                    ∗ (ind_owned when the indirect block exists)
                    ∗ link_auth Γ i (nlink n.rec) (type of n.rec)
                    ∗ ⌜local clauses⌝
rec_owned  Γ i dn  := byte_range Γ (IBLOCK i) (64·slot i) (dinode_bytes dn)
blk_owned  Γ b bs  := byte_range Γ b 0 bs
byte_range Γ b off bs := [∗ list] k ↦ v ∈ bs, Γ.Φ (b·BSIZE + off + k) v
```

* The inode node ranges over **every nonzero `addrs` entry, regardless of
  `rec.size`** (an inode may own blocks beyond its size — `itrunc` frees them
  all, `writei`'s partial-failure commit leaves one).  The abstract byte
  sequence is a **READING, not the ownership**:
  `fn_file_bytes n := take rec.size (concat blocks)`;
  `dir_entries n := dir_view (fn_file_bytes n)`.  Distinctness of an inode's
  own blocks is the `∗`.
* **Local clauses of `inode_owned`**: type ∈ {DIR,FILE,DEV}; size ≤ MAXFILE;
  `bm_covers`; `type = 0 → nlink = 0`; `nlink ≤ 32767`; of a DIRECTORY,
  `16 ∣ size`, `"."` ↦ self and `".."` present, names unique.  **There is NO
  clause at `fs_inodes` or `fs_state` level.**  The dots clauses are GUARDED
  by `fn_nlink n ≠ 0`, because this kernel has two size-0 `T_DIR` records: the
  claim box `ialloc` installs and the corpse `itrunc` leaves.
* `fn_bare` is the shape all three contentless records share (addrs all zero,
  entries zero, size 0, nlink 0) and `inode_owned_bare_move` is the ONE mover
  for both the claim box and the corpse.

**Mid-transaction states are NOT "inconsistent views"** — a block `balloc` took
that no inode points at yet is a piece CHECKED OUT of `fs_state Γ_L`, exactly
as a locked inode is.  Consequence: no abstract target state, no pure
well-formedness projection, and **no per-operation finalize obligation at
`end_op`**.  An operation's entire contribution is the sequence of LOCAL steps
at its AUs.

### D.4 The share, the split, and where the abstract map's authority lives

`fs_state Γ dq S` puts every BYTE at `dq` while the ghost column stays WHOLE.
**The share stops at the factoring**: `inode_owned = inode_phi ∗ inode_ghost`,
lifted to `fs_state Γ dq S ⊣⊢ fs_footprint Γ dq S ∗ fs_ghost Γ S`, and
`fs_ghost` is Φ-free and therefore share-free — "half a `link_auth` is not half
a file system, it is an unusable element".  That is what makes the resource
transport `FsDurXfer.fs_state_xfer` provable at any `q > 1/2` (it ALLOCATES a
fresh `Γ'` and reads the disjointness off the source's own exclusivity; nothing
is computed from `S`).

**The abstract map's AUTHORITY is not part of `fs_state`** — it travels beside
it, inside `FsDurSnap.fs_snap` on the durable side and inside
`InodeRegion.ftop_inv` on the era's.  A checked-out holder holds the FRAGMENT
`top_frag_q Γ dq i n`; **a read-locker holds a QUARTER of it, and that one line
is what makes a read lock a read lock** (every mover of the abstract map needs
the whole element).

`fs_state` has a fourth PURE conjunct `fs_geom S` — four rows (`fg_sbok`,
`fg_reg`, `fg_regdom`, `fg_dirloc`) — and they are the ONE thing §0's local
rule cannot supply: nothing per-inode can say how the inode MAP and the
SUPERBLOCK fit together.

### D.5 Link counts and types are ONE RA — the type register (§6½)

Per inode, at `γlink`: `auth (gmultiset ity)` with `ity := TFile | TDir (p : Z)`.
The AUTHORITY is a uniform multiset `(nlink + [type = DIR]) · {[ty]}`, parked
in the inode-region invariant beside the record and tied to it.  FRAGMENTS are
`{[ty]}`, **one per counted dirent**; validity gives agreement (a fragment's
element IS the target's current type) and `#fragments ≤ multiplicity` at once.
Retyping is legal exactly at multiplicity 0 (the inode is free).  **The link
count IS the fragment count: there is no separate count RA.**

Which dirents carry what: a NAME record for target `t` holds
`∃ ty, {[ty]} at t ∗ ⌜∀ p, ty = TDir p → p = d⌝`; `.` is the inode's own
self-fragment (the `+1` xv6 does not count, and what ties a directory's `..`
DATA to its type); `..` is an ordinary fragment of the PARENT's register
asserting nothing; an orphan's `..` holds NONE — it was returned when the
parent's entry for it was removed.  The per-directory exactness clause is
`nlink = #{name records whose fragment is TDir _} + [nlink ≠ 0]`, i.e. xv6's
own accounting.  **`iget`'s licence is the reading**: a dirent's fragment at
`t` ⟹ multiplicity ≥ 1 ⟹ `nlink + [DIR] ≥ 1` ⟹ `t` is allocated.

`fs_links_valid` (gather the whole family into one `own`, apply `own_valid`) is
the ONLY place the cross-inode fact "#tokens ≤ nlink everywhere" is produced;
it is never a clause and never maintained.

> A per-holder link LEDGER, with its `wl/wdu/wdt/g/p` columns, its parent tie
> and its flavour index, **does not exist and must not come back**: its columns
> were not a function of the image's bytes, so no boot could produce them.

### D.6 The on-disk image and the block layer's ghost state

`fs-ghost-state.md` §1's organizing line is **HOME BLOCK vs LOG-REGION BLOCK**
(`fs_home_set cov logstart = cov ∖ log_region_set logstart`):

* `fsblock (fs_bytes γfs) bno bs` — a run of BSIZE `ghost_map Z (bv 8)`
  elements at `DfracOwn 1`.  **This is what every home-block owner above the
  log holds**: the bitmap block and free pool, block 1's park,
  `ireg_recs`/`ireg_blk`, the icache escrow's payloads, the boot bundle.
* `fs_chalf γfs bno bs` — half of `bno ↪[fs_cache γfs] bs`, the PARKED half of
  the cache entry.  Only two kinds of holder are left: the log's own storage,
  and a handle's MACHINERY half carried out of a bio payload.  **A HOME
  block's parked half lives inside `fs_bytes_inv` and no mortal ever holds
  one.**
* `fs_bytes_inv gL gc gX home Xv` at `fsbN` (a child of `logN`) — the tie: the
  byte auth, the home blocks' parked cache halves, `bytes_tie`, `bytes_dom`,
  and the EXCEPTION SET `X` (nonempty only in the recovery window of a dirty
  header; `initlog` SEALS it empty and the seal is what every runtime reader
  takes).
* Membership is DERIVED, not threaded: `fsblock_home` reads `b ∈ home` off the
  byte auth and `bytes_dom`, so no consumer above the log ever names a
  `gset Z`.  The home-set-free row `fs_bytes_any γfs` is what everything
  carries — on the three persistent invariant carriers (`log_ctx`,
  `bitmap_inv`, `ireg_inv`), because the row contains an `inv` and is not
  timeless while `ireg_blk`/`bitmap_res`/`blk_res` all must be.

**The fraction story:** `fsΦ` takes a leading `dfrac`; `fsblock_ne_full`
(fraction 1 against ANY share) is the resource reading of "a read-locker cannot
write", and `fsblock_ne_34` (¾ against ¾) is why **two read-locked inodes
cannot be holding one block** — which is why a read-locker's withdrawal is a
QUARTER and not a half.

**Sealing is not optional:** `fsblock` and `inode_blocks` are
`Typeclasses Opaque`, because a bare `iFrame` at a goal holding a 1024-element
`big_sepL` under two `Definition`s unfolds and does not come back (measured: a
`bitmap_res_close` past ten minutes; an unsealed `ic_rd_arm` `Timeless`
instance ran nineteen minutes).  A `Typeclasses Opaque` seal is **not** crossed
by a `reflexivity` equation, so crossings go through explicit wands
(`fsblock_q_1_of`/`_to`, …), one `iDestruct` each.

### D.7 How the inode / bitmap / directory views hang off it

* **inode**, in-era: `FsStateEra.inode_owned_era Γ γi inum n` is §2's
  `inode_owned` as a checked-out holder carries it — `rec_owned` is replaced by
  `InodeRegion.dinode_at` (the holder's exclusive record PROXY) and the era's
  abstract value rides beside it as `top_frag`.
* **bitmap**: `bitmap_res` IS `FsStateBitmap.free_bitmap_at` at
  `FsBytesGamma.fs_gamma_L`.  One predicate, two instances.
* **directory**: there is no separate `dir_owned` predicate — a directory's
  tokens live INSIDE `inode_owned` (as `ent_toks Γ n`, empty for a
  non-directory), because `fs_inodes` is the one `∗` over `inode_owned` and
  tokens hung off a sibling would sit outside `fs_state` entirely.
  `dir_owned Γ sb d n := inode_owned Γ sb d n ∗ ⌜fn_is_dir n = true⌝` is the
  READING.  Both dirent deltas come out of `FsTree` at the RECORD view
  (`dir_zeroed_at`, `dir_insert_at`); `dir_view_insert` needs no
  `dir_names_unique` (an insert only has to reach the FRONT of the first-match
  scan, unlike a removal, which unmasks whatever was hiding behind it).

### D.8 The eventual friendly layer (recorded, not built)

`fs-friendly.md` + `fs-fragments.md`: the abstract state is an inum-keyed node
store with a distinguished root (`fs_nodes : gmap Z fsnode`, `fs_root`),
**not** an inductive tree — forced four times over (every landed inum-indexed
resource is `Z`-keyed; files are multi-parent; `".."` must be IN `ents` or
`dirlookup(dp,"..")` has nothing to hand `iget`; no rename ⟹ no tree surgery).
"Dirs form a tree" is a derived pure predicate, a separate conjunct, never a
property of the type.  Target style: Perennial/GoNFS logically-atomic triples
`⟨t. fs_rep t⟩ create(p,ty) ⟨t'. fs_rep t' ∗ ⌜t' = tree_insert t p (fresh ty)⌝⟩`,
which is natural here because `wp_log_write_au` and the `ireg_*_au` accessors
are already the same HOCAP/atomic-update shape.

---

## 2b(E) THE LOG / TRANSACTION DISCIPLINE — AND THE CRASH-LAYER QUESTION

### E.1 What a caller inside `begin_op` / `end_op` holds

`begin_op` mints, `end_op` consumes:

```coq
log_tx γ   := ∃ t, t ↪[ln_tx γ] ()          (* the open-transaction token *)
log_op γ u := log_opb γ u ∗ log_tx γ        (* budget half + the token     *)
```

`log_opb γ u` is `u` units of write budget — the pre-transaction `log_op`
verbatim, which is why no callee below it moved.  **The transaction id is
EXISTENTIAL and no client names it**: `log_res` ties the ledger to the open
transactions by CARDINALITY, not identity, so an ending transaction never has
to say what it touched.  `log_tx_halve`/`log_tx_join` let an arm name the id
for the length of a park and put it straight back.

The set-form family, introduced by fs-icache §18 and extended by §G.19–§G.25:

| form | meaning |
|---|---|
| `log_opS γ u Sb` | "I am inside an op with `u` units of budget and write-set `Sb`" (closed form) |
| `log_opSe γ u Sb e0` | the OPEN / epoch-indexed form: `(∃ i, i ↪[ln_ops γ] (u,Sb,e0)) ∗ log_epoch_lb γ e0 ∗ ⌜1 ≤ e0⌝` |
| `log_opSw` / `log_opSwe` | the mid-write variants (`log_opSwe` is the primitive) |
| `log_opSt γ u Sb` | `log_opS ∗ log_tx` — namex's shape, because namex must hold the token at each per-level `ilock` |
| `log_credit γ cr Sb e0 b` | `if cr then ⌜b ∈ Sb⌝ ∨ (∃ e, logged_at γ e b ∗ ⌜e0 ≤ e⌝) else emp` — persistent and timeless in both arms |

**A SHARE of the `ln_tx` element is what every file-system-side park spells**,
through the one atom `TxPin.tx_pin γ t q` with `tx_pin_o` (a column that may be
empty) and `tx_pins` (a ledger).  There are eight such parks (the escrow's
`DepTx` arm and `ic_out_frz`, `ic_pin_tx`, the pool's `ipool_transit` and
`crp_row`, and the region's `ireg_fpin`/`ireg_cpin`/`ireg_parked`), and the
three refutations `tx_pin_no_ops` / `tx_pin_o_no_ops` / `tx_pins_no_ops`
against an EMPTY `ln_tx` authority are what "no transaction is open" buys the
commit.  `(t,q)` are always FIELDS of whatever records the park, never
existentials inside it — two halves of one element are not the whole.

### E.2 What `log_write` requires

`SpecLogWrite.wp_log_write_au_range_body` is the form the whole-function proof
proves; **every other form is derived from it**.  Pre:

* a budget unit: `log_opSe γ (S u) Sb e0` (or `log_op γ (S u)` in the counted
  form), plus `log_credit γ cr Sb e0 b` when the caller claims absorption;
* the bio handle from the caller's own `bread`
  (`bio_held … bs_new bsd (Clean bs_old)`, or `Dirty` for a re-log);
* **the caller's byte elements for the range it changed, at fraction 1** —
  `byte_range (fs_bytes γfs) bno off sub_old` with `⌜length sub_old = len⌝`
  (the whole-block corollary surrenders an `fsblock`);
* `⌜home-range bno⌝`.

Post: `log_opS γ u (Sb ∪ {[bno]})`, `bio_locked … (Dirty bs_new)`, and the byte
elements back at the new value.  **Nothing is owed beyond the bytes it writes**
— no pure fact is re-established, and the three AU forms carry no payload-step
premise.  The writer's ONE obligation is the splice shape
`length bs = BSIZE → length bsl = BSIZE → length sub_new = len ∧
bs = blk_splice off sub_new bsl`, *guarded by the block's width, because the
width is nameable only inside the handle* — which is why `wp_log_write_au` is a
COROLLARY (`off := 0`, `len := BSIZE`) rather than a second whole-function
proof.

Byte-range granularity is what lets a writer owning an inode record's 64 bytes
(or a dirent's 16) `log_write` the whole buffer: **the other 960 bytes are
never presented**; `byte_range_log_update` learns them from the log's own tie.
`lw_au_rec` is the record-slot corollary the inode region uses.

Both `log_write` panics are dead: "too big a transaction" (a unit in hand ⟹
`n < LOGBLOCKS`) and "outside of trans" (`op_tok` vs `ops_auth` ⟹ `out ≥ 1`).

### E.3 Budget, credits and absorption

* **The unit is always consumed**, whether the block is new (`i = lh.n`:
  `bpin`'s `bref` → the Dirty slot, `γdirty` flip, `n++`) or absorbed
  (`bno ∈ W`: no bpin, the unit simply burned).  "Callers reason with
  `MAXOPBLOCKS` worst case exactly like the C code does."
* **Spend-at-most is forced above the log.**  `bmap` has premise `5 ≤ n`, pre
  `log_op γ n`, post `∃ n', ⌜n − 5 ≤ n' ≤ n⌝ ∗ log_op γ n'`.  The reason
  generalises to every function above the log that does not take `log.lock`:
  `log_op` is a `ghost_map` element whose only mover is `ghost_map_update`
  against the ledger auth inside `log_res`, behind the log spinlock.  On the
  direct-hit path bmap reaches its epilogue still holding every unit and
  **cannot burn the surplus**; a spend-exactly post would require minting.
  State the premise as a lower bound (`5 ≤ n`), not as `5 + u`, so a `writei`
  loop can present its counter directly.  `bfree` by contrast is
  spend-EXACTLY, and `balloc`'s arm-dependent budget is free because its post
  is already a two-arm disjunction.
* **Group-wide absorption** is the epoch design: `log_write` charges a unit per
  call, but `itrunc` frees up to 269 blocks that all hit ONE bitmap block, so
  `lh.n` grows by 2 against an accounting that demands 270.  "The kernel is
  correct; the accounting was wrong."  The fix is a positive, client-held claim
  at the granularity of a whole OPEN GROUP: epoch-indexed witnesses that
  **self-invalidate** (a commit advances the epoch, so nothing has to be
  revoked); the receipt lives in the inode region's invariant (keyed by inum,
  so no per-generation gate); the credit is a RESOURCE whose credited arm
  RECORDS rather than no-ops ("an arm that quietly skipped the spend could not
  prove it had not also skipped the append"); the birth epoch is threaded
  SYNTACTICALLY because a contract boundary erases it; the ties are AMBIENT
  (`icfg_log`/`icfg_ist`) because a counted contract cannot carry them.
* **The walk is ONE unit, whatever the path length**, indexed by the success
  arm.  Three of the walk's five `iput` sites cannot be credited but all three
  are TERMINAL.  The loop invariant needs an UNCONDITIONAL
  `iput_units ≤ ncur` clause beside the guarded one.

### E.4 What the WAL exposes, and what it does not

> **THE LOG'S LOCK RESOURCE CARRIES NO CLIENT PROPOSITION.**  There is no
> parked client payload, no payload index and no client law about a write: a
> `log_write` proves nothing about the file system, so nothing
> file-system-shaped is threaded through the ~75 files that name `log_ctx`,
> and that context is arity-fixed.

`log_ctx` carries: the sealed "log" lock, the two frozen cells, the era's swap
receipt, `fs_bytes_at` (the byte view's invariant), `SbPark.sb_parked` (block
1, OWNED at fraction 1 with its parse), `LogSnapLaw.snap_law` (the file
system's own commit law), and `FsBlocks.exc_sealed` (recovery is over).  All
four FS-facing conjuncts are resources or persistent laws; none is a payload
the log re-indexes at a write.

**`end_op` has no FS-facing premise and no FS-facing postcondition.**

Block 1 being owned at fraction 1 makes "block 1 is never logged" a
REFUTATION, not a premise (`log_write`'s window is at fraction 1 too, so a
write to `SB_BNO` meets two full owners of one byte).  `sbN` is a SIBLING of
`fsbN`, not a child, because the commit holds the byte view open while the
collection reads block 1.

### E.5 The crash layer — the direct answer

**Can `balloc`, `bmap`, `writei`, `ialloc`, `iupdate`, `itrunc`, `dirlink` be
proved with NO crash layer at all?  YES.**

Machine-checked evidence, from the tree at HEAD:

```
$ grep -ciE 'FsCrash|gen_cert|crash_seam|disk_seq_permit|P_fs|fr_D|riscv_crash' \
      Spec{Balloc,Bfree,Bmap,Dirlink,Dirlookup,Ialloc,Iget,Ilock,Iunlock,
           Iupdate,Iput,Itrunc,Namex,Readi,Writei,BeginOp,LogWrite}.v
  -> 0 for every one of them
$ ... same grep on SpecFsinit.v -> 11 ;  SpecEndOp.v -> 9
```

**Exactly two contracts in the whole file system mention the crash layer:
`SpecEndOp` and `SpecFsinit`.**  No fs.c function's statement names
`FsCrash.P_fs`, `fr_D`, `gen_cert`, `fs_crash_seam`, `disk_seq_permit`, or a
generation.  Structurally this is by design:

* the crash predicate's durable half is `FsDurSnap.P_dur D`, a function of the
  committed map `D` alone over EXISTENTIAL gnames closed inside `crashN`; a
  writer **holds no durable write permission, owes no deferred justification,
  and re-establishes nothing about the durable side at its own step**;
* `D` moves at exactly one instant, `write_head`'s disk write at `n > 0`, and
  it does so through a **permit whose premises are the log's own rows and
  NOTHING of the client's**.  The install arithmetic never leaves `FsCrash.v`:
  "pictures, write sets and slot indices do not appear above `SpecEndOp`";
* "Mid-batch inconsistency of `L` never matters, because `D` only ever jumps at
  a batch boundary, where `outstanding = 0`.  FS-level consistency is not a
  parameter any more and not a per-op wand."

**What a Lean port must therefore provide instead of a crash layer**: an
opaque persistent `log_ctx` bundle (the lock, the byte-view invariant row,
block 1's park, and — as an opaque persistent atom — the commit law), plus
`begin_op`/`end_op`/`log_write` contracts in the shapes of §E.1–§E.2.  Then
`balloc`, `bfree`, `bmap`, `ialloc`, `iupdate`, `writei`, `readi`, `itrunc`,
`dirlink`, `dirlookup`, `namex`, `iget`/`ilock`/`iunlock`/`iput` all go through
unchanged.

**What is lost, exactly, and nothing more:**

1. **The end-to-end durability theorem.**  Without `FsCrash`, `end_op` cannot
   be given a contract that says the committed view moved to `L` on the home
   set, and `SystemAdequacy.xv6_power_adequacy` (the machine is never stuck
   under any interleaving of power cycles, hart steps and device steps) has no
   statement.  You keep per-function partial correctness; you lose "and this
   survives a power cycle".
2. **`initlog`'s recovery proof and `fsinit`'s boot story.**  Recovery is
   general in `n` only because `FsCrash.hdr_wf` is carried across the power
   cycle by the crash predicate itself.  Without the layer, recovery becomes an
   assumption and `initlog` needs a clean-image premise back.
3. **The exception set.**  `exc_own`/`exc_sealed` exist solely to make the
   era's byte view mintable at the COMMITTED view while the cache still reads
   crashed bytes.  With no crash layer there is no dirty-header boot and the
   seal is vacuous — every reader's shape is unchanged either way, since every
   reader already takes the seal and immediately turns it into `X = ∅`.
4. **A build-cone caveat, not a statement caveat.**  `LogInv.log_ctx` *does*
   name `FsCrash.fs_crash_seam_at` and `FsCrash.fs_bank` internally, and
   `LogSnapLaw` requires `FsCrash`.  So the fs specs' dependency CONE touches
   the crash layer even though their STATEMENTS do not.  In a Lean port this
   is the seam to cut: make those two conjuncts of `log_ctx` opaque
   parameters, and the fs.c layer never notices.

One thing that is **not** lost: the transaction discipline itself.  `log_tx`,
the eight `tx_pin` parks, the budget, the credits and the epoch are all
WAL-internal and FS-side machinery with no crash content — `tx_pin_no_ops` and
friends are about an empty `ln_tx` authority, not about power.

---

## 2b(F) THE SPEC-MODULE CONVENTION

### F.1 The four files

For each kernel function `F`: `Code<F>.v`, `Spec<F>.v`, `Proof<F>.v`,
`Link<F>.v`.  The motivating rule:

> A whole-function WP proof must NOT depend on its callees' *proofs* — only on
> their *specs*.  Otherwise the build serializes along the kernel call graph
> and no amount of `-j` helps.

* **`Spec<F>.v`** — the public interface: a `Definition wp_<f>_<variant>_body
  … := … -∗ WP (Loop) {{ Φ }}` plus a `Module Type F` whose `Parameter`
  restates the BINDER LIST (not the statement) and concludes with the `_body`.
  It requires only the definitional layer — **never** a `Proof*` file and
  **never** a `Code*` file, its own included.  Spec files compile in ~2 s.
* **`Proof<F>.v`** — a **sealed functor** over its callees' interfaces
  (`Module FProof (A : ASPEC) (B : BSPEC) : F.`).  The lemma keeps its original
  header and its first tactic is `cbv beta delta [wp_<f>_<variant>_body].`
  (not `intros`/`hnf`/`unfold`: head reduction would zeta-reduce the
  statement's `let`-chain away and the original `intros` would fail).
* **`Link<F>.v`** — one line, the only file where a proof meets its callees'
  proofs: `Module F := FProof A B.`  It must APPLY the functor, not
  re-abstract it, not re-ascribe it, and not inline the proof.
  `Require Import Link*` may appear ONLY in a `Link*.v`.

Why exactly this: functor application is free (Rocq substitutes, it does not
re-typecheck); seal with `:` so the link `.vo` is ~4 KB and the body is pruned;
**the statement lives only in the `_body` `Definition`** so signature and proof
cannot drift; the `Parameter`'s restated binders are load-bearing because Rocq
reads argument scopes and implicit-argument status off the head constant's
type.

An **assumed callee** still gets the full shape: `Module Type` in the Spec, and
an `Axiom` *inside a module* in the Link (`Module Kerneltrap : KERNELTRAP.
Axiom …  End Kerneltrap.`) — not `Declare Module`, because the coverage tool
finds axioms by scanning for the keyword.

The shape breaks only where a function's proof needs ITSELF one call deeper
(`forkret_park`): there the knot is tied in the LOGIC instead — a persistent
`park_token` defined as a guarded fixpoint, proved once at the top.

### F.2 THE SUFFIX DECODER

A function's `Spec<F>.v` may publish several `_body` definitions.  They are
**one proof, several published forms**, each derived from the strongest by a
few lines, with the weaker ones kept **byte-stable** so no existing caller's
arity or statement moves.  The suffixes compose, e.g.
`wp_iunlockput_dep_gen_body`, `wp_iupdate_credgen_body`.

| suffix | means | quotable source |
|---|---|---|
| **`_sconf`** | the ordinary whole-function contract, stated over the **S-mode configuration bundle** `IntrDefs.sconf` (hw config, `cur_privilege = Supervisor`, mstatus + the SIE ghost half, `mie = MIE_S` pinned, `menvcfg = MENVCFG_S`) together with `sie_cap_gpr` and `callee_saved`. **This is the baseline form; every other suffix is a variant of it.** `sconf_at ms` is the mstatus-exposing accessor flavour, for boundaries only. |
| **`_gen`** | the **SET-FORM / generalised** contract of fs-icache §18: the op-wide write-set `Sb` is threaded (`log_opS γ u Sb` in, `Sb'` with `⌜Sb ⊆ Sb'⌝` out) instead of only a unit count. "`wp_<f>_sconf` is this with the set forgotten, derived at the `log_op` existential's own witness — so no existing caller moves." Needed because monotonicity of the set is what a caller (writei, create) needs across a callee that runs on EVERY returning path. In `SpecAcquire` the same suffix means "generalised over the lock tier", i.e. the general reading of a narrower landed form — **`_gen` always means "the weaker/landed form is an instance of this"**. |
| **`_cred`** | **credited**: the contract carries the absorption boolean `cru`/`crb`/`crd` so a caller that knows the block is already in this op's write set pays 0 instead of 1. "This is `SpecLogWrite.wp_log_write_gen`'s own `cr` device lifted through a straight-line function; `wp_iupdate_gen` is this at `cru := false`, so no existing caller moves." Its existence is forced: `CreateBudget.cr_budget_needs_inode_credit` is the machine-checked refutation of doing without. |
| **`_credgen`** | credited **and** epoch-indexed, with the enabled-base premise dropped: `wp_iupdate_cred_body` with `eb = true` removed, both complements threaded, and — since fs-log §G.4 — the credit taken as a RESOURCE against a NAMED birth epoch rather than as a pure own-set premise. **"It is the STRONGEST of the four and the other three are derived from it"** (`_cred` = this at `eb := true`; `_gen` = this at `cru := false`; `_sconf` = `_gen` at the `log_op` existential's witness), each derivation three lines, all four statements byte-stable. |
| **`_link` / `_unlink`** | `SpecIupdate` only. The **link-minting** (fs-icache §20.18 stage C2) and **link-spending** (stage C4) contracts: `_link` is `_credgen` cut to create's altitude (`cru`-credited, `eb := true`) with the added premise `di_type dn ≠ 0` — forced, not chosen, because (L3) says a type-0 record has `nlink = 0` while the flush makes it ≥ 1, so a type-0 `dn` makes the region's closing clause FALSE. `_unlink` is the dual, carrying the zero-receipt's two ambient ties on the paying route and nothing on the vacuous route. Each is a further POSITIONAL parameter so no landed caller's arity moves. |
| **`_dep`** | **deposit-descriptor-generic**: the body takes `(d : ic_dep)` as a parameter and publishes whichever escrow OUT arm `d` names (`DepTx` = the write arm, which parks a transaction share; `DepRd` = the read arm, which leaves three quarters of the bundle in the escrow). "ONE proof of ilock's code, three arms, selected by `d` BEFORE the call and published at the checkout's own ghost step — so no bundleless out-state stands between the contract's post and a later arming fupd." |
| **`_tx`** | the **transactional** instance of `_dep` at `DepTx`: it CONSUMES `LogInv.log_tx icfg_log` and PRODUCES `IcacheEscrow.ic_tx_dep`. "ONE C FUNCTION, ONE PROOF, TWO PUBLISHED FORMS, selected by what the caller holds… `ProofIlock` proves it by DERIVATION from the generic form (`wp_ilock_tx_of_dep`); not a line of ilock's own proof is re-run." |
| **`_noalloc`** | a **second contract over one function**, at a premise that kills the allocation arms. `BMAP_NOALLOC` adds `blkmap_get bm fbn ≠ 0`, and then "the contract drops EVERYTHING the allocation arms needed": no `log_op` and no budget premise, no `log_ctx` and hence no `γ : log_names` at all, `bslot` rather than `bslots 3` — and the postcondition is exact rather than existential. Both contracts come from ONE proof body (`ProofBmap.BmapCore`, parameterised by whether the allocation arms are live). Precedent: `SpecWalk`'s `WALK` / `WALK_NOALLOC`. |
| **`_root`** | a **disjoint REGIME of the same code**, not an instance. `wp_namex_root_body` is `namex("/", 0, name)`: a path of exactly one `'/'` has no elements, so nothing reads a disk block, nothing takes a sleeplock and nothing can park. "The general contract above is a contract about a WALK… None of that holds of the one caller that matters at BOOT." `userinit` runs before there is a current process, before `fsinit` has read the superblock and before any transaction exists. **The corner assumes strictly less** — in particular it does NOT take `ireg_open`, the sealed regime, which does not exist before fsinit has run: "a premise that cannot be satisfied by the one caller is not a premise, it is a hole." |
| **`Era` / `_era`** | the same function's contract at the **abstract-FS "era trace"** (`FsAbs*`, the programmer-friendly cursor view), so a caller never has to reach past a wrapper into the walk. `SpecNparWrapEra` is to `SpecNparEra` exactly what `SpecNameiEra` is to `SpecNamexEra`. The diff against the counted contract is one trace premise (`FsAbsStart.ep_start`), a success arm that exposes the returned inum at the cursor's parent index, and a failure arm that gains `np_dead`. **The counted contract has no era twin**, "for the reason the namei-side era files have none: a counted continuation has no `P` to hand the cursor to." |

Two conventions worth porting with the suffixes:

* **Add a variant as a further POSITIONAL parameter, never by widening an
  existing one** — "so no existing caller's arity moves (`ProofWritei` applies
  `wp_iupdate_gen` positionally)", and the landed contracts stay byte-stable.
* **`Notation K_<f> := (n%nat)`** lives in the Spec file beside the body and is
  the frame-depth budget (`K_ilock = 66`, `K_bmap = 56`, `K_balloc = 50`,
  `K_bfree = 44`, `K_namex_root = 74`), computed as the function's own frame
  slots plus its deepest callee's `K`.  `bslots bn n` is the bio-reference
  budget and is often exactly tight (bmap's 3 is the peak at the second
  `balloc`).
---

# 3. Spec shapes — verbatim

Everything below is byte-exact Coq from `/shared/xv6rocq/iris/`. Line ranges are given so
you can re-extract with `sed -n 'A,Bp'`.

## 3.0 How to read these — the contract-variant suffix decoder

Every fs function's `Spec<F>.v` defines one or more `wp_<f>_<variant>_body` *definitions*
(the contract, stated as a curried chain of `->` premises and `-∗` resources ending in a
continuation `-∗ WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang)`), and then a `Module Type <F>` whose
`Parameter`s are the universally-quantified forms of those bodies. `Proof<F>.v` provides the
functor; `Link<F>.v` applies it. The suffixes:

| suffix | meaning |
|---|---|
| `_sconf_` | the ordinary S-mode whole-function contract (the default form; same naming as `wp_swtch_sconf`, `wp_panic_sconf` elsewhere in the tree) |
| `_gen_` | the **credited / generic** form: carries the log's *already-logged set* through the contract so repeated `log_write`s of the same block **absorb** instead of costing a unit each. `_sconf_` is `_gen_` at `cr = false` with the set forgotten. |
| `_dep_` | generic over the icache checkout **descriptor** `d : ic_dep` — the caller picks `DepRd` (read-locker) or `DepTx` (transactional locker) |
| `_tx_` | the `DepTx` reading of `_dep_`: caller brings `LogInv.log_tx icfg_log`, contract produces `IcacheEscrow.ic_tx_dep`. Derived, not re-proved (`wp_ilock_tx_of_dep`). |
| `_cred_`, `_credgen_` | `iupdate`'s credited forms (with/without the generic set) |
| `_link_`, `_unlink_` | `iupdate`'s two nlink-delta forms, for `sys_link` / `sys_unlink` |
| `_noalloc_` | `bmap`'s second contract, for a caller that cannot allocate (`readi`, which runs **outside** a transaction). Under `bv_unsigned (blkmap_get bm fbn) <> 0` all three balloc arms are dead. |
| `_root_` | `namex`/`namei` specialised to the path `"/"`; only callee is `iget`. Used by the boot client. |
| `_era_` | the application/trace-"era" contract of the walk, consumed by the `FsAbs*`/`App*` layer. **Not needed for a kernel-only port.** |

**Who is inside a transaction.** `begin_op`/`end_op` bracketing shows up as the caller
holding `LogInv.log_op` (an open op) and, for the credited forms, a budget + already-logged
set. As a rule:

* **must be inside a transaction** (consume/produce `log_op`, and call `log_write`):
  `balloc`, `bfree`, `ialloc`, `iupdate`, `bmap` (allocating form), `itrunc`, `writei`,
  `dirlink`, and `iput` when it frees.
* **must NOT need a transaction**: `readi`, `bmap_noalloc`, `dirlookup`, `namecmp`, `stati`,
  `iget`, `idup`, `iunlock`.
* **either side, selected by descriptor**: `ilock`, `iunlock`, `iunlockput` (`_dep_` vs `_tx_`).
* **opens its own transaction**: `ireclaim` (it calls `begin_op`/`end_op` itself), and
  `fsinit` (via `initlog` + `ireclaim`).
* **buffer resources**: every function that calls `bread` states a `bslot` budget (the
  bio-layer's reference slots) and returns it via `brelse`. `ilock` states "ONE `bslot`:
  bread's reference, which brelse gives back"; `fsinit` needs `bslots 35`
  (`(LOGBLOCKS + 2) + 2 + 1`) and returns `bslots 3`.

## 3.1 `fsinit` (and the inlined `readsb`) — superblock geometry + contract

**`SpecFsinit.v:202-556`** — the superblock cell addresses, FSMAGIC, sb_image, wp_fsinit_sconf_body, Module Type FSINIT

```coq
(* ===================================================================== *)
(*  THE SUPERBLOCK: ITS EIGHT CELLS, ITS 32 BYTES, AND ITS MAGIC          *)
(*                                                                        *)
(*  This is the ONLY superblock abstraction in the tree, and it exists    *)
(*  only because fsinit is the only function that touches the record as   *)
(*  a whole -- [li a2,32] at +0x16 is [sizeof(struct superblock)] and the *)
(*  [memmove] at +0x26 writes all 32 bytes at once.  Every other contract *)
(*  keeps taking its one field as a bare fractional cell; nothing below   *)
(*  this file changes.                                                    *)
(* ===================================================================== *)

(* fs.h's layout, as eight 32-bit fields.  The four that already have names
   elsewhere ARE these addresses: [BitmapInv.sb_size] is [sb + 4],
   [InodeInv.sb_ninodes] is [sb + 12], [InodeInv.sb_inodestart] is [sb + 24]
   and [BitmapInv.sb_bmapstart] is [sb + 28].  The other four are named here
   because fsinit is what brings them into existence. *)
Definition sb_base : mword 64 := mword_of_int KernelSyms.sb.
Definition sb_magic    : mword 64 := pa_add sb_base 0.
Definition sb_nblocks  : mword 64 := pa_add sb_base 8.
Definition sb_nlog     : mword 64 := pa_add sb_base 16.
Definition sb_logstart : mword 64 := pa_add sb_base 20.

Lemma sb_size_addr      : BitmapInv.sb_size      = pa_add sb_base 4.
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.
Lemma sb_ninodes_addr   : InodeInv.sb_ninodes    = pa_add sb_base 12.
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.
Lemma sb_inodestart_addr : InodeInv.sb_inodestart = pa_add sb_base 24.
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.
Lemma sb_bmapstart_addr : BitmapInv.sb_bmapstart = pa_add sb_base 28.
Proof. reflexivity. Qed.

(* [lui a5,0x10203 / addi a5,a5,64] at +0x38/+0x3c *)
Definition FSMAGIC : Z := 0x10203040.

(* THE IMAGE'S BLOCK 1, as the 32 bytes the memmove reads.  Stated with
   [BlockWords.word_bytes] rather than an inverse decode so that the premise
   below is an EQUATION ON BYTES the proof can rewrite with, not a
   proposition it has to invert. *)
Definition sb_image (magic fssize nblocks ninodes
                     nlog logstart inodestart bmapstart : mword 32)
    : list (bv 8) :=
  word_bytes magic ++ word_bytes fssize ++
  word_bytes nblocks ++ word_bytes ninodes ++
  word_bytes nlog ++ word_bytes logstart ++
  word_bytes inodestart ++ word_bytes bmapstart.

Lemma sb_image_length (magic fssize nblocks ninodes
                       nlog logstart inodestart bmapstart : mword 32) :
  length (sb_image magic fssize nblocks ninodes
                   nlog logstart inodestart bmapstart) = 32%nat.
Proof.
  rewrite /sb_image !length_app !word_bytes_length. reflexivity.
Qed.

Definition wp_fsinit_sconf_body
    `{!riscvGS Σ, !xv6G Σ, !bioslotG Σ, !fdslotG Σ,
      ICFG : icfg, APP : appcfg Σ, FSC : fscfg, !irefslotG Σ, !pavG Σ, !wchG Σ} `{GEN : GenId} `{CID : CpuId} `{XI : CurCtx}
    (γs : list gname) (j : nat) (γl : gname)          (* the running process *)
  (* disk fabric + lock  *)
    (pd pav pu : mword 64)
    (* ---- the image's block 1, field by field ---- *)
    (v_magic v_size v_nblocks v_ninodes v_nlog
     v_logstart v_inodestart v_bmapstart : mword 32)
    (bs_sb : list (bv 8))
    (sb_old : nat -> bv 8)                     (* the .bss bytes memmove kills *)
    (* ---- initlog's own bundle, threaded verbatim ---- *)
    (bs_hdr : list (bv 8))
    (* THE BYTE VIEW'S RECORD ON THE EXCEPTION SET (durable-disk lane
       E-except): what the era's logged view holds at the pending home
       blocks.  Threaded straight into [initlog]. *)
    (Xv : Z -> list (bv 8))
    (M : log_mirror)            (* the era's BORN-TRUE picture (1a) *)
    (L : gmap Z (list (bv 8))) (D : gmap Z bool)
    (vlock : mword 32) (vname vcpu : mword 64)
    (v_start v_dev v_nc v_n : mword 32)
    (pidv : mword 32) (dq : dfrac)
    (m : regfile) (K : nat) (eb : bool)
    (b : bool) (lks : gset string) (Upr : ustate)
    (* ---- the record block 1's bytes decode to (durable-disk lane C-3a) ---- *)
    (sbrec : fs_sb) :=
  let pcE : mword 64 := mword_of_int KernelSyms.fsinit in
  let pj := proc_addr j in
  let ret_tgt := ret_pc (m !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 1 : mword 5)) in
  (K_fsinit <= K)%nat ->
  (* ---- bread's / the log's block-number arithmetic ---- *)
  log_geom_ok fsc_cov fsc_logst ->
  (* THE SUPERBLOCK'S OWN BLOCK: block 1, covered, and not log storage *)
  (1 : Z) ∈ fsc_cov ->
  ~ ((1 : Z) ∈ log_region_set fsc_logst) ->
  (* ================================================================== *)
  (*  THE IMAGE PREMISES.  Everything below is a claim about what mkfs   *)
  (*  wrote into block 1, threaded from the boot client exactly as       *)
  (*  IcacheBoot's allocated-inum bundles are.  This is the family the   *)
  (*  N4b / N4d / N5a / N5c ledgers have been parking here.              *)
  (* ================================================================== *)
  (* (a) the block IS a superblock: its first 32 bytes are the eight
         fields, in fs.h's order *)
  take 32 bs_sb = sb_image v_magic v_size v_nblocks v_ninodes
                           v_nlog v_logstart v_inodestart v_bmapstart ->
  (* (a') ...AND THE RECORD THEY DECODE TO (durable-disk lane C-3a).  Block
         1's run stops being dropped at fsinit's return: it goes down into
         [initlog], which parks it in [SbPark.sbN] and seals the handle into
         [LogInv.log_ctx], so the commit's collection can finally say what
         block 1 holds.  These two premises are what the park is stated at,
         and both are read off the boot image (W1 of
         [FsCfgBoot.fs_boot_image_wf]) rather than recomputed. *)
  fs_parse_sb (fun _ => bs_sb) = Some sbrec ->
  fs_sb_ok sbrec ->
  (* (a'') THE COLLECTION'S GEOMETRY AND THE TWO FIELD TIES (durable-disk
          C-8).  fsinit's invariants are stated at the CONFIG numbers and
          the durable snapshot at the record block 1 DECODES to; these are
          the bridge, and [FsCollect.cg_ist] is the third tie.  All three
          come off [FirstTok.first_fsinit_pures], where the region's width
          tie that [cg_reg] rests on actually lives -- see that file.  They
          are consumed here and nowhere else: fsinit builds the file
          system's law out of the invariants it already holds and hands it
          to [initlog], which parks it in [LogInv.log_ctx]. *)
  col_geom sbrec icfg_ist icfg_nib (fs_home_set fsc_cov fsc_logst) ->
  FsImg.sb_bmapstart sbrec = fsc_bmapstart ->
  FsImg.sb_size sbrec = fsc_size ->
  (* (b) the magic, which is what refutes the LIVE panic arm at +0x40 *)
  bv_unsigned v_magic = FSMAGIC ->
  (* (c) the three field values every fs contract downstream reads *)
  v_ninodes = (mword_of_int fsc_ninodes : mword 32) ->
  v_inodestart = (mword_of_int icfg_ist : mword 32) ->
  v_bmapstart = (mword_of_int fsc_bmapstart : mword 32) ->
  v_logstart = (mword_of_int fsc_logst : mword 32) ->
  (* (d) THE THREE ninodes TIES -- SpecIalloc's and SpecIreclaim's, finally
         stated about a real record.  [ninodes <= 16 * nib] is the one that
         existed nowhere in the tree before (N5c). *)
  1 < fsc_ninodes ->
  fsc_ninodes <= 16 * Z.of_nat icfg_nib ->
  fsc_ninodes < 2 ^ 31 ->
  icfg_dev = ROOTDEV ->
  (0 < icfg_nib)%nat ->
  (* (f) the inode region's block geometry, and itrunc's, threaded to
         ireclaim *)
  0 <= icfg_ist ->
  ireg_blocks_ok icfg_ist icfg_nib fsc_cov fsc_logst ->
  0 < fsc_size <= BPB ->
  0 <= fsc_bmapstart ->
  fsc_bmapstart ∈ fsc_cov ->
  ~ (fsc_bmapstart ∈ log_region_set fsc_logst) ->
  cov_below fsc_cov fsc_size ->
  (* (g) THE ON-DISK HEADER IS WELL FORMED, AND THAT IS ALL (durable-disk
         lane E-except; the CLEAN-IMAGE premise [hdr_n bs_hdr = 0] IS GONE).
         These are [FsCrash.hdr_wf]'s three clauses at the header block's
         content, plus its block-1 row: the decoded write set is bounded by
         the log region, duplicate-free, and names covered HOME blocks other
         than the superblock.  At a clean image the decode is empty and all
         of them are trivial; at a real crash they are what the durable
         header invariant delivers, and recovery is what consumes them --
         [initlog]'s copy loop runs, [install_trans] lands every entry (and
         SHRINKS the byte view's exception set as it goes), and the closing
         [write_head] clears the log. *)
  ((hdr_dec bs_hdr).1 <= LOGBLOCKS)%nat ->
  NoDup (hdr_dec bs_hdr).2 ->
  (forall b : Z, b ∈ (hdr_dec bs_hdr).2 ->
     b ∈ fsc_cov /\ b ∉ log_region_set fsc_logst /\ b <> FsImg.SB_BNO) ->
  (* (g'') THE EXCEPTION SET'S VALUES ARE THE SLOTS' (durable-disk lane
         E-except), threaded verbatim into [initlog]. *)
  (forall (i : nat) (b : Z),
     (hdr_dec bs_hdr).2 !! i = Some b ->
     Xv b = lm_view M (log_slot_bno fsc_logst i)) ->
  (* (g') THE ERA'S TWO READINGS OF ONE IMAGE (durable-disk 1a): the logged
         view and the era's born-true mirror agree on the covered range.
         Threaded verbatim into [initlog], where it is what makes the boot
         [log_state] pack's row (b) provable. *)
  (forall b : Z, b ∈ fsc_cov -> L !! b = Some (lm_view M b)) ->
  (* ---- ireclaim's printk, as a hypothesis and not a functor ---- *)
  (j < NPROC)%nat ->
  γs !! j = Some γl ->
  (* a0 = dev *)
  m !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 10 : mword 5) = (sign_extend' 64 icfg_dev : mword 64) ->
  (* fsinit's cone: its own bread/brelse ("bcache", 4), initlog
     ("bcache", 4) and ireclaim ("itable", 2) -- "itable" is the lowest,
     so one premise there covers the whole cone via [locks_below_mono]. *)
  locks_below lks "log" ->
  sie_cap_gpr KT1 m K b pj -∗
  cpu_own 0 eb pj b lks -∗
  (* THE TRAP-CSR COMPLEMENT, in and out.  fsinit takes no lock of its own,
     so nothing here mints the pay its sleeping callees (bread, initlog,
     ireclaim) need; it threads the caller's.  [emp] at [eb = true], the real
     pair at [eb = false] -- which is the index forkret's [if (first)] arm
     reaches it at, since this revision's scheduler leaves [intena = 0].
     claude-notes/completed/eb-generic-sweep.md is the recipe. *)
  trap_csrs_ext KT1 eb -∗
  cpu_claim_ext eb pj -∗
  kernel_text -∗ kernel_data -∗ pc_is pcE -∗
  printk_env fsc_printk fsc_uart fsc_disk -∗
  bio_ctx fsc_bio (fs_view fsc_fs fsc_disk icfg_dev fsc_cov) -∗
  (* THE CRASH SEAM AT THE APPLICATION'S GUEST, AND THE TRANSPORT
     (app-instances.md round C), both off kit 2: fsinit builds the commit's
     law from them ([FsCollectAll.fs_snap_law_build], which produces the
     snapshot AND the application's durable claim beside it) and derives
     initlog's arity-free seam from the first.  Then the era certificate
     and the era's BORN-TRUE mirror half + swap receipt (durable-disk 1a). *)
  fs_crash_seam_at app_guest fsc_cov fsc_logst -∗
  app_xfer -∗
  gen_cert -∗
  log_mirror_born M -∗
  (* THE LOG'S FOUR GNAMES, AT THEIR GENESIS VALUES, AND THEY ARE
     [icfg_log]'s.  Threaded straight into [initlog] at +0x4e, which fills
     them rather than minting its own.  See the header: this is the
     conjunct that makes fsinit's post assemble into [FsReady.fs_ready]. *)
  log_free_tok icfg_log -∗
  (* ================================================================== *)
  (*  THE SUPERBLOCK, BEFORE AND AFTER                                   *)
  (* ================================================================== *)
  (* IN: block 1's client half, which is what pins the bytes bread returns
     to the image; and 32 bytes of RAW .bss at [&sb], which is all the
     superblock is until +0x26 runs. *)
  (* THE BYTE VIEW'S ROW, NAMED (durable-disk lane E-except): fsinit
     spends it twice -- at the [readsb] crossing above +0x4e, which runs
     BEFORE recovery and so goes through the [b ∉ X] form, and inside
     [initlog], which is where the exception set is emptied and sealed. *)
  fs_bytes_inv (fs_bytes fsc_fs) (fs_cache fsc_fs) (fs_exc fsc_fs)
               (fs_home_set fsc_cov fsc_logst) Xv -∗
  fsblock (fs_bytes fsc_fs) 1 bs_sb -∗
  (* THE BYTE VIEW'S EXCEPTION HANDLE (durable-disk lane E-except), from
     the era's mint, threaded straight into [initlog], which empties it and
     seals it into [LogInv.log_ctx].  fsinit itself spends it once, at the
     [readsb] crossing above +0x4e: block 1 is never in the exception set
     ([FsCrash.hdr_wf]'s block-1 row, lane E-blk1).  It is [∅] while the
     era's mint still reads the RAW home blocks. *)
  exc_own (fs_exc fsc_fs) (list_to_set (hdr_dec bs_hdr).2) -∗
  ([∗ list] i ∈ seq 0 32, pa_add sb_base i ↦ₘ sb_old i) -∗
  (* ---- the icache's four persistent things, straight from
         [IcacheBoot.icache_boot] ---- *)
  ireg_reg fsc_ireg fsc_fs icfg_ist icfg_nib -∗
  (* THE BOOT-SHELTER TOKEN (fs-fragments.md §7.12), from [icfg_alloc] through
     the boot chain: fsinit frames it across bread/memmove/initlog and hands it
     to ireclaim, which is the only reason it is safe there (§7.1.7).  Returned
     in the post, so the boot caller can seal it to [ireg_open] after fsinit
     returns and before [kexec("/init")] -- that seal is OWED to forkret's
     first branch. *)
  ireg_boot -∗
  is_itable2 fsc_itlock fsc_ic fsc_fs fsc_ireg fsc_cov fsc_logst icfg_nib icfg_dev -∗
  itable_inv -∗
  ic_escrows fsc_ic fsc_fs fsc_ireg fsc_cov fsc_logst -∗
  ic_sleeplocks fsc_ic -∗
  (* itrunc's bitmap, through ireclaim's iput *)
  bitmap_reg fsc_fs fsc_bmapstart fsc_cov fsc_logst fsc_size -∗
  (* ---- initlog's RAW struct log cells, threaded straight through ---- *)
  log_addr ↦₄ vlock -∗
  lock_name_field log_addr ↦₈ vname -∗
  lock_cpu log_addr ↦₈ vcpu -∗
  l_start ↦₄ v_start -∗
  l_dev ↦₄ v_dev -∗
  l_out ↦₄ (mword_of_int 0 : mword 32) -∗
  l_cmt ↦₄ (mword_of_int 0 : mword 32) -∗
  l_ncommit ↦₄ v_nc -∗
  lh_n_pa ↦₄ v_n -∗
  ([∗ list] i ∈ seq 0 LOGBLOCKS, ∃ w : mword 32, lh_block i ↦₄ w) -∗
  (* ---- initlog's FsBlocks material ---- *)
  ghost_map_auth (fs_cache fsc_fs) 1 L -∗
  ghost_map_auth (fs_dirty fsc_fs) 1 D -∗
  ([∗ set] z ∈ fsc_cov, z ↪[fs_dirty fsc_fs]{#(1/2)} false) -∗
  fs_chalf fsc_fs (log_hdr_bno fsc_logst) bs_hdr -∗
  ([∗ list] i ∈ seq 0 LOGBLOCKS,
     ∃ bs : list (bv 8), fs_chalf fsc_fs (log_slot_bno fsc_logst i) bs) -∗
  (* the caller's own pid cell *)
  proc_priv_bare pj pidv Upr -∗
  (* the running-thread bundle and the disk fabric *)
  procs_inv γs -∗
  dev_inv fsc_uart fsc_disk -∗
  disk_geom fsc_disk pd pav pu -∗
  is_lock fsc_dlock d_lock "virtio_disk"%string (disk_res_at fsc_disk pd pav pu) -∗
  (* THIRTY-FIVE slot units.  initlog seals 32 of them into [log_state]'s
     pool and returns two; ireclaim needs three; so ONE is held back across
     the [jal initlog] at +0x4e.  See the header. *)
  bslots ((LOGBLOCKS + 2) + 2 + 1)%nat -∗
  (* ONE ledger unit for ireclaim's iget/iput pair; it comes back *)
  iref_slot -∗
  (* THE CROSSING IS THE LITERAL [true], NOT [b].  This function can SLEEP
     (its bread / ilock / bwrite does), and a park moves the hart with
     interrupts off, so the crossing has nothing to do with SIE -- the
     porting guide's "a PARKING function's [wp_next] index is [true]
     UNCONDITIONALLY".  Spelled [b] the two coincide at the only instance
     the [eb = true] premise admits, which is why this went unnoticed; once
     [eb = false] is reachable the [b] form would promise the caller it
     comes back on the hart it called from, which a park makes false. *)
  wp_next true pj (fun (CID : CpuId) =>
  ∀ (mf : regfile),
      ⌜callee_saved m mf⌝ -∗
      sie_cap_gpr KT1 mf K b pj -∗
      cpu_own 0 eb pj b lks -∗
      trap_csrs_ext KT1 eb -∗
      cpu_claim_ext eb pj -∗
      pc_is ret_tgt -∗
      proc_priv_bare pj pidv Upr -∗
      (* ================================================================ *)
      (*  THE EIGHT CELLS ARE BORN.  This is the whole point of the        *)
      (*  contract: the caller handed in 32 raw .bss bytes and gets back   *)
      (*  the typed fields every other fs contract in the tree takes as a  *)
      (*  premise, at the image's values.  [sb_size], [sb_ninodes],        *)
      (*  [sb_inodestart] and [sb_bmapstart] are literally the same        *)
      (*  addresses BitmapInv.v and InodeInv.v already name.               *)
      (* ================================================================ *)
      sb_magic ↦₄ v_magic -∗
      BitmapInv.sb_size ↦₄ v_size -∗
      sb_nblocks ↦₄ v_nblocks -∗
      InodeInv.sb_ninodes ↦₄ (mword_of_int fsc_ninodes : mword 32) -∗
      sb_nlog ↦₄ v_nlog -∗
      sb_logstart ↦₄ (mword_of_int fsc_logst : mword 32) -∗
      InodeInv.sb_inodestart ↦₄ (mword_of_int icfg_ist : mword 32) -∗
      BitmapInv.sb_bmapstart ↦₄ (mword_of_int fsc_bmapstart : mword 32) -∗
      (* NOTHING COMES BACK FOR BLOCK 1 (durable-disk lane C-3a).  The run
         used to be returned here and DROPPED by forkret; it is now spent
         inside, into [initlog]'s [SbPark] park, and rides out as a conjunct
         of the [log_ctx] below. *)
      (* THE LOG LAYER, BUILT by initlog at +0x4e and already USED by
         ireclaim at +0x54.  It does not cross the boundary as an input.
         AT [icfg_log], not existentially: this is [FsReady.fs_ready]'s log
         conjunct, modulo the seal site's instantiation of [bn]/[fsc_fs]/[fsc_cov]/
         [fsc_logst] at [fsc_bio]/[fsc_fs]/[fsc_cov]/[fsc_logst] -- the
         device it is stated at IS [icfg_dev] since rank 1c. *)
      log_ctx icfg_log fsc_bio fsc_fs fsc_cov fsc_logst icfg_dev -∗
      (* three, not two: see the header *)
      bslots 3 -∗
      iref_slot -∗
      (* the boot-shelter token, handed back for the seal (fs-fragments.md
         §7.12) *)
      ireg_boot -∗
      WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang)) -∗
  WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang).

Module Type FSINIT.
  Parameter wp_fsinit_sconf :
    forall `{!riscvGS Σ, !xv6G Σ, !bioslotG Σ, !fdslotG Σ,
             ICFG : icfg, APP : appcfg Σ, FSC : fscfg, !irefslotG Σ, !pavG Σ, !wchG Σ} `{GEN : GenId} `{CID : CpuId} `{XI : CurCtx}
      (γs : list gname) (j : nat) (γl : gname)
      (pd pav pu : mword 64)
      (v_magic v_size v_nblocks v_ninodes v_nlog
       v_logstart v_inodestart v_bmapstart : mword 32)
      (bs_sb : list (bv 8))
      (sb_old : nat -> bv 8)
      (bs_hdr : list (bv 8))
      (Xv : Z -> list (bv 8))
      (M : log_mirror)
      (L : gmap Z (list (bv 8))) (D : gmap Z bool)
      (vlock : mword 32) (vname vcpu : mword 64)
      (v_start v_dev v_nc v_n : mword 32)
      (pidv : mword 32) (dq : dfrac)
      (m : regfile) (K : nat) (eb : bool)
      (b : bool) (lks : gset string) (Upr : ustate)
      (sbrec : fs_sb),
      wp_fsinit_sconf_body γs j γl pd pav pu


                           v_magic v_size v_nblocks v_ninodes v_nlog
                           v_logstart v_inodestart v_bmapstart bs_sb sb_old
                           bs_hdr Xv M L D vlock vname vcpu v_start v_dev v_nc v_n
                           pidv dq m K eb b lks Upr sbrec.
End FSINIT.
```

## 3.2 `iinit`

**`SpecIinit.v:40-112`** — itable geometry (NINODE, stride 136, lock bases, name strings) + wp_iinit_sconf_body + Module Type IINIT

```coq
(*  itable geometry (file.h / fs.h, corroborated by the disassembly)    *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

(* struct itable { struct spinlock lock; struct inode inode[NINODE]; }, so the
   lock is the FIRST member and &itable.lock = &itable. *)
Definition itable_addr : mword 64 := mword_of_int KernelSyms.itable.

Definition NINODE : nat := 50%nat.

(* sizeof(struct inode) = 136 (the loop's [addi s1,s1,136]); the array starts
   at itable+24, just past the 24-byte spinlock, and the sleeplock sits at
   offset 16 in struct inode (past dev/inum/ref plus padding).  So the
   sleeplock of inode [i] is at itable+40+136*i -- the cursor the loop walks
   from [inode_lock 0] up to the end pointer [inode_lock NINODE]. *)
Definition inode_stride : Z := 136.
Definition inode_lock_base : Z := KernelSyms.itable + 40.
Definition inode_lock (i : nat) : mword 64 := acur inode_lock_base inode_stride i.

(* the side conditions [ArrCursor]'s cursor lemmas take, discharged once. *)
Lemma inode_lock_base_nonneg : 0 <= inode_lock_base.
Proof. unfold inode_lock_base, KernelSyms.itable. lia. Qed.
Lemma inode_stride_pos : 0 < inode_stride.
Proof. unfold inode_stride. lia. Qed.
Lemma inode_lock_end_fits : inode_lock_base + inode_stride * Z.of_nat NINODE < 2 ^ 64.
Proof.
  unfold inode_lock_base, inode_stride, NINODE, KernelSyms.itable.
  assert (H : (2 ^ 64 = 18446744073709551616)%Z) by (vm_compute; reflexivity).
  rewrite H. lia.
Qed.

(* the two string literals iinit passes on -- "itable" to initlock and "inode"
   to every initsleeplock.  Both sit in .rodata past etext with no ELF symbol
   of their own, so they are spelled out here; the proof reads their bytes out
   of [kernel_data] with [kernel_data_string]. *)
Definition itable_name_str : Z := 0x80007448.
Definition inode_name_str : Z := 0x80007450.

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

Definition wp_iinit_sconf_body `{!riscvGS Σ, !xv6G Σ} `{GEN : GenId} `{CID : CpuId} `{XI : CurCtx} (m : regfile) (K : nat)
    (vlock : mword 32) (vname vcpu : mword 64) (b : bool) (p : mword 64) :=
  let pcE : mword 64 := mword_of_int KernelSyms.iinit in
  let ret_tgt := ret_pc (m !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 1 : mword 5)) in
  let lk : mword 64 := itable_addr in
  let c_name := lock_name_field lk in
  let c_cpu := add_vec lk (sign_extend' 64 (mword_of_int 16 : mword 12)) in
  (* iinit's own frame is 6 slots and its deepest callee (initsleeplock) wants
     6 more below that. *)
  (12 <= K)%nat ->
  sie_cap_gpr KT1 m K b p -∗
  kernel_text -∗ kernel_data -∗ pc_is pcE -∗
  lk ↦₄ vlock -∗
  c_name ↦₈ vname -∗
  c_cpu ↦₈ vcpu -∗
  ([∗ list] i ∈ seq 0 NINODE, sl_raw (inode_lock i)) -∗
  wp_next b p (fun (CID : CpuId) =>
    ∀ mr,
    sie_cap_gpr KT1 mr K b p -∗
    pc_is ret_tgt -∗
    ⌜ callee_saved m mr ⌝ -∗
    lk ↦₄ (mword_of_int 0 : mword 32) -∗
    lock_name lk "itable"%string -∗
    WpLock.lk_cpu_ready lk -∗
```

## 3.3 `balloc`

**`SpecBalloc.v:132-254`** — K_balloc and wp_balloc_sconf_body

```coq
Notation K_balloc := (72%nat) (only parsing).
Definition wp_balloc_sconf_body
    `{!riscvGS Σ, !xv6G Σ, !bioslotG Σ, !fdslotG Σ, !irefslotG Σ, !pavG Σ, !wchG Σ} `{GEN : GenId} `{CID : CpuId} `{XI : CurCtx}
    
    (γs : list gname) (j : nat) (γl : gname)          (* the running process *)
    (γu : uart_names) (γd : disk_names) (γk : gname)  (* disk fabric + lock  *)
    (pd pav pu : mword 64)
    (bn : bio_names)
    (γ : log_names) (γfs : fs_names)
    (cov : gset Z) (logstart : Z) (bmapstart : Z) (size : Z) (dev : mword 32)
    (γpr : gname)
    (u : nat)
    (pidv : mword 32) (dq dqb dqs : dfrac)
    (m : regfile) (K : nat) (eb : bool)
    (b : bool) (lks : gset string) (Upr : ustate) :=
  let pcE : mword 64 := mword_of_int KernelSyms.balloc in
  let pj := proc_addr j in
  let ret_tgt := ret_pc (m !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 1 : mword 5)) in
  (K_balloc <= K)%nat ->
  (* the covered range's block-number bounds (bread's 2^31 arithmetic
     premise, and 0 is never a client block) and the fact that the log's
     own storage is covered *)
  log_geom_ok cov logstart ->
  (* THE OUT-OF-BLOCKS ARM'S CALLEE, as a hypothesis and not a functor -- see
     the header for why that is what keeps this proof at the standing six *)
  (* ONE BITMAP BLOCK (see the header), and the [0 < size] that kills the
     +0x12 arm *)
  0 < size <= BPB ->
  (* the bitmap block is a covered HOME block: bread's premise, and
     log_write's *)
  0 <= bmapstart ->
  bmapstart ∈ cov ->
  ~ (bmapstart ∈ log_region_set logstart) ->
  (j < NPROC)%nat ->
  γs !! j = Some γl ->
  (* the uint argument arrives sign-extended (RV64 ABI) *)
  m !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 10 : mword 5) = sign_extend' 64 dev ->
  (* the order premise, at the LOWEST rank this cone touches; every
     higher one follows by [locks_below_mono]. *)
  locks_below lks "log" ->
  sie_cap_gpr KT1 m K b pj -∗
  cpu_own 0 eb pj b lks -∗
  (* THE TRAP-CSR COMPLEMENT, NOT THE BARE PAIR.  balloc holds no lock of its
     own -- every push_off/pop_off pair that can mint or spend an
     [arm_pay 0 eb _] lives inside bread (and, through it, acquiresleep /
     virtio_disk_rw), so balloc is a PURE PASS-THROUGH: it neither mints nor
     spends this complement itself, only threads it down to each bread call
     and takes it back from bread's continuation.  At [eb = true] the
     complement is [emp], so no existing caller gains an obligation; at
     [eb = false] it is the honest pair, held by the caller because the TRAP
     handed it over, and passed to bread exactly as bread's own contract
     wants it.  See claude-notes/completed/sched-hart-generic.md and
     claude-notes/completed/eb-generic-sweep.md. *)
  trap_csrs_ext KT1 eb -∗
  cpu_claim_ext eb pj -∗
  kernel_text -∗ pc_is pcE -∗
  (* the general printk path's two PERSISTENT credentials, for the
     out-of-blocks arm *)
  kernel_data -∗
  printk_env γpr γu γd -∗
  bio_ctx bn (fs_view γfs γd dev cov) -∗
  log_ctx γ bn γfs cov logstart dev -∗
  (* the caller's own pid cell (bread's acquiresleep records it) *)
  proc_priv_bare pj pidv Upr -∗
  (* the two superblock fields, read at +0x0a and +0xa0 and never written *)
  sb_size ↦₄{dqs} (mword_of_int size : mword 32) -∗
  sb_bmapstart ↦₄{dqb} (mword_of_int bmapstart : mword 32) -∗
  (* THE BITMAP'S INVARIANT (BitmapInv.v): persistent; the pool is inside *)
  bitmap_inv γfs bmapstart cov logstart size -∗
  (* the running-thread bundle *)
  procs_inv γs -∗
  (* the disk fabric *)
  dev_inv γu γd -∗
  disk_geom γd pd pav pu -∗
  is_lock γk d_lock "virtio_disk"%string (disk_res_at γd pd pav pu) -∗
  (* TWO slot units: the bitmap buffer is bread and log_written (log_write
     wants a free unit for its bpin) before it is brelsed, and bzero then
     does the same for the data block. *)
  bslots 2 -∗
  (* this operation's reservation, at least the two units a success costs *)
  log_op γ (2 + u) -∗
  (* THE CROSSING IS THE LITERAL [true], NOT [b].  This function can SLEEP
     (its bread / ilock / bwrite does), and a park moves the hart with
     interrupts off, so the crossing has nothing to do with SIE -- the
     porting guide's "a PARKING function's [wp_next] index is [true]
     UNCONDITIONALLY".  Spelled [b] the two coincide at the only instance
     the [eb = true] premise admits, which is why this went unnoticed; once
     [eb = false] is reachable the [b] form would promise the caller it
     comes back on the hart it called from, which a park makes false. *)
  wp_next true pj (fun (CID : CpuId) =>
  ∀ (mf : regfile),
      ⌜callee_saved m mf⌝ -∗
      sie_cap_gpr KT1 mf K b pj -∗
      cpu_own 0 eb pj b lks -∗
      trap_csrs_ext KT1 eb -∗
      cpu_claim_ext eb pj -∗
      pc_is ret_tgt -∗
      proc_priv_bare pj pidv Upr -∗
      sb_size ↦₄{dqs} (mword_of_int size : mword 32) -∗
      sb_bmapstart ↦₄{dqb} (mword_of_int bmapstart : mword 32) -∗
      bslots 2 -∗
      ((* FAILURE: a0 = 0, nothing allocated, nothing spent, the bitmap
          unchanged -- every bit below size was already set *)
       (⌜mf !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 10 : mword 5) = (mword_of_int 0 : mword 64)⌝ ∗
        log_op γ (2 + u))
       ∨
       (* SUCCESS: a0 = a nonzero covered home block, zeroed, two units gone *)
       (∃ blk : mword 32,
          ⌜mf !!! Regidx (mword_of_int 10 : mword 5) = sign_extend' 64 blk⌝ ∗
          ⌜bv_unsigned blk <> 0⌝ ∗
          ⌜bv_unsigned blk ∈ cov⌝ ∗
          ⌜~ (bv_unsigned blk ∈ log_region_set logstart)⌝ ∗
          (* THE FRESHNESS CLAIM IS THE RUN ITSELF.  The byte view is
             EXCLUSIVE, so a caller that also holds one run per block its own
             structures name learns, by [FsBlocks.fsblock_ne], that this
             block is none of them -- which is exactly what re-establishes
             [InodeInv.blkmap_wf]'s injectivity at an insertion (see
             [InodeInv.inode_fresh]).  Without it bmap is unprovable. *)
          fsblock (fs_bytes γfs) (bv_unsigned blk) (replicate BSIZE (bv_0 8)) ∗
          log_op γ u)) -∗
      WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang)) -∗
  WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang).

```

**`SpecBalloc.v:255-281`** — why the credited form exists (the absorption argument) — READ THIS

```coq
(* ===================================================================== *)
(*  THE CREDITED FORM -- balloc's contract with the LOG'S ALREADY-LOGGED  *)
(*  SET carried through it, [SpecBfree.wp_bfree_gen]'s shape verbatim.    *)
(* ===================================================================== *)

(* WHY.  balloc log_writes exactly TWO blocks, and a caller that is
   allocating several blocks in one transaction pays far less than
   [2 * blocks] for them:

   - THE BITMAP BLOCK.  [BBLOCK] collapses to [bmapstart] for every
     allocatable block ([WriteiBudget.one_bitmap_block], from this
     contract's own [0 < size <= BPB] premise), so EVERY balloc of the
     transaction log_writes THE SAME block.  Only the first pays; the rest
     absorb.  That is what [cr] claims, exactly as in bfree.

   - THE FRESH BLOCK, log_written by the inlined bzero at +0x4c.  It is
     never credited (a freshly allocated block cannot already be in this
     op's set in any way the caller can know), so it always costs one --
     but the caller LEARNS the block is now in the set, and can therefore
     absorb its OWN later log_write of the very same block.  That is the
     data-block absorption without which a four-block chunk of writei does
     not fit MAXOPBLOCKS ([WriteiBudget.wi_cost_noabs_busts]).

   The FAILURE arm log_writes nothing, so both the budget and the set come
   back untouched.  [wp_balloc_sconf] is this at [cr = false] with the set
   forgotten, and is unchanged: every existing caller keeps threading
   [log_op]. *)
```

```coq
    (pidv : mword 32) (dq dqb : dfrac)

     premise, and 0 is never a client block) and the fact that the log's own
     storage is covered *)

     BBLOCK collapses and the outer geometry never appears *)

  panic_env -∗

  (* THE BLOCK BEING FREED: its EXCLUSIVE byte run.  Holding it is what

      sie_cap_gpr KT1 mf K b pj -∗
      cpu_own 0 eb pj b lks -∗
      trap_csrs_ext KT1 eb -∗
      cpu_claim_ext eb pj -∗
      pc_is ret_tgt -∗
      proc_priv_bare pj pidv Upr -∗
      sb_bmapstart ↦₄{dqb} (mword_of_int bmapstart : mword 32) -∗
      bslots 2 -∗
      log_op γ u -∗
      WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang)) -∗
  WP (Loop : expr riscv_lang).

Module Type BFREE.
  (* THE CREDITED / GENERAL FORM; [wp_bfree_sconf] below is its
```
