## 6.1  CROSS-CUTTING THEMES

Twenty recurring warnings, grouped.  Each names the files that state it; the
verbatim text is in the per-function sections below.

### T1. Dead arms are REFUTED, never "proved" — and each refutation names its premise

This is the single most repeated sentence in the cone.  A branch the C can
syntactically reach but the contract's premises make unreachable is discharged
by deriving `False` from the branch condition, *not* by giving the arm a
postcondition.  The Rocq headers are careful to say "refuted, not proved"
(`ProofBalloc.v`, `ProofBfree.v`, `ProofBmap.v`, `SpecBfree.v`).

Complete inventory of dead arms, with the premise that kills each:

| function | instruction | arm | killed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| balloc | `+0x12 beqz a5,+0xf6` | `sb.size == 0` → printk, skipping the s2..s8 restore | `0 < size` |
| balloc | `+0x98` fall-through | a second OUTER loop iteration | `size <= BPB` (FSSIZE 2000 < BPB 8192) |
| bfree | `+0x3a c.beqz` | `panic("freeing free block")` | caller's EXCLUSIVE byte run vs the free pool (`FsStateBitmap.free_pool_used`) |
| bmap | `+0xb2` | `panic("bmap: out of range")` | `fbn < MAXFILE` bounds the `bltu a5,a4` at `+0x044` |
| dirlookup | `+0x1c` | `panic("dirlookup not DIR")` | `di_type dn = T_DIR` premise |
| dirlink | `+0x60` | `panic("dirlink read")` (the loop readi) | `dlk_rd_clamp_full` under the OLD granularity premise — see T16, this arm is now LIVE |
| fsinit | `+0x40 bne a4,a5` | `panic("invalid file system")` | IMAGE premise `sb_magic (sb_image …) = FSMAGIC` |
| ialloc | `+0x12 bgeu a5,a4` | empty-region exit, printk without pushing s1..s6 | `1 < ninodes` |
| ilock | `+0x0e` | `ip == 0` half of `panic("ilock")` | `ientry_unsigned`: the address is `itable + 24 + 136k`, never 0 |
| ilock | `+0x12` | `ip->ref < 1` half | `IcacheInv.iref_live_load_au` over the caller's LIVENESS SLICE |
| iunlock | three tests | `panic("iunlock")` | slot address ≠ 0; liveness slice; the holder's own sleeplock bundle |
| ireclaim | `+0x0a bgeu a5,a4` | empty-region exit through the SECOND `c.jr ra` at `+0xc6`, **frame never pushed** | `1 < ninodes` |
| ireclaim | `+0x50 beq s3,zero` | the C's `if(ip)` | **iget's POSTCONDITION** (`ientry_ne_zero`) — "the one refutation in this cone that a caller cannot see" |
| readi | `+0x026 bltu a4,a3` | xv6's `off + n < off` overflow test | joint numeric premise `off + n < 2^32` |
| readi | `+0x088 c.beqz a0` | "bmap found no block" break (and its whole target block `+0xce..+0xd6`, never proved) | `InodeInv.bm_covers` |
| writei | `+0x02e` | the overflow test | joint numeric premise `off + n < 2^31` |
| writei | the `-1` break | `either_copyin` failing on the KERNEL arm | `SpecEitherCopyin`'s post is a bare `r = 0` when `¬user` |
| namex | `+0xf8..+0x102` | a block gcc emitted that re-tests two bytes already decided | pure code fact |
| namex | `+0x116..+0x11a` | the `len = 0` entry | unreachable from the above |
| namex(era) | `L_par`, nameiparent tail of `L_done` | | `a1 = 0` at the namei side |
| itrunc | — | no panic on any path | callees' panics refuted in their own proofs |

**Port rule.** Budget a `False.elim`-shaped obligation per dead arm and keep the
premise that kills it in the spec, or the arm reappears.  Several premises exist
*only* to kill an arm (`0 < size`, `1 < ninodes`, `di_type dn = T_DIR`,
`off + n < 2^32`).

### T2. The FOUR live panic arms — partial correctness, and that is deliberate

`ProofIlock.v` calls its `ip->type == 0` arm **"the first proof here that takes
a panic branch on purpose"**.  The pattern, restated in four headers:

1. **`ilock: no type`** (`+0x9c`) — the pool legitimately holds free inodes, and
   "allocatedness is namei/ialloc's knowledge, future work".
2. **`iget: no inodes`** (branch `+0x6a`, call at `+0x9e` — *after* the
   epilogue) — "whether the table is full is a fact about every OTHER process's
   open files", so no caller premise could rule it out.  Note it fires **while
   iget HOLDS itable.lock**, which is what the `n + 3 < 2^31` premise and the
   rank-table edge `"itable" < "pr"` pay for (`LinkIget.v`).
3. **`dirlookup read`** (`+0x46`) — became live when the granularity premise was
   retired (T16).
4. **`dirlink read`** (`+0x68`) — same cause.

In every case the header says the same three things: the arm **DIVERGES through
`SpecPanic`'s own contract**; the postcondition therefore **speaks only for the
calls that return**; and that is **sound in a partial-correctness WP and is the
honest statement**.  `SpecDirlookup.v` adds the subtle consequence:

> No postcondition arm is added: panic never returns, so the found/notfound
> arms carry an implicit "...and every readi in the scan returned 16", which is
> what the old premise gave and what the panic arm gives without it.

**Port rule.** A Lean port keeps the same trick only if its WP is
partial-correctness.  Do not try to give a live panic arm a postcondition.

### T3. Panic *credentials* are threaded even where every arm is dead

`kernel_data` / `panic_env` / `γpr` ride through contracts whose own panics are
all refuted, because a **callee's** panic arm wants them (balloc takes them for
printk; bfree takes them "because bread's own interior panic arm wants one";
bmap "because the interior acquire's own holding-check arm wants a panic
contract regardless"; fsinit, ialloc, ireclaim, namex, namei, nameiparent all
say some version of this).  `LinkX.v` headers consistently state whether a
`Panic` functor is instantiated.

Two arms in this kernel that stock xv6 panics on are `printk` instead:
**balloc's "out of blocks"** and **ialloc's "no inodes"** — the GENERAL printk
path, not the panic path, "at balloc time `panicking` is 0".  `SpecDirlookup.v`
records that this is the *cause* of the granularity retirement (T16):

> THIS kernel's balloc returns 0 when the disk is full (stock xv6 panics -- see
> SpecBalloc.v's header), so dirlink's third arm really does append a PREFIX of
> a 16-byte record and leaves `size = 16*nrec + tot` permanently non-granular.

### T4. Inside vs outside a log transaction — and the no-allocation bmap

The sharpest "does not / cannot" in the cone is `SpecReadi.v`:

> readi calls bmap, and bmap ALLOCATES when the slot is zero -- which calls
> log_write.  But fileread does not wrap readi in a transaction, so an
> allocating read would hit `panic("log_write outside of trans")`.  It never
> happens because every block below a file's size is allocated, and
> `InodeInv.bm_covers` is that statement.

Consequences to port:
* bmap has **two contracts**: `BMAP` and `BMAP_NOALLOC` (`SpecBmap.v:771`,
  `LinkBmapNoalloc.v`).  readi links against the second; writei against the first.
* `bm_covers` is a **premise for readi and a POSTCONDITION for writei** —
  "a caller that writes and then reads could never re-establish it unless writei
  promised it".
* `ireclaim` mints and retires its own reservation inside the loop body, so
  **no `log_op` crosses its contract boundary in either direction**.
* `fsinit`'s call ORDER is load-bearing: initlog *produces* `log_ctx`,
  ireclaim *consumes* it, so the log context is not an input at all.
* `dirlink` "runs INSIDE A TRANSACTION (writei's bmap can allocate)".

### T5. The log budget: spend-exactly vs spend-at-most, and WHY

Stated three times, in identical words (`SpecBmap.v`, `SpecBfree.v`,
`SpecIupdate.v`):

> bmap **cannot** promise to have spent five, because it has no way to BURN a
> surplus -- `log_op` moves only through the ledger authority inside log.lock,
> which bmap never takes -- and on the direct-hit path it does no balloc and no
> log_write at all.

So: **straight-line functions that always log** (bfree, iupdate) get
spend-EXACTLY `log_op (S u)` → `log_op u`.  **Anything that branches** (bmap,
writei, itrunc, iput, namex, dirlink) gets a spend-at-most INTERVAL.

Absorption is the other half, and it is what makes two proofs possible at all:

* **itrunc**: 269 `bfree`s + 1 `iupdate` would be 270 units against
  `MAXOPBLOCKS = 10`.  `FSSIZE = 2000 < BPB = 8192` ⇒ exactly ONE bitmap block
  ⇒ the log absorbs every free after the first ⇒ true cost **2**.  The loop
  invariant is `bm_paid γ bmapstart 1`, a **disjunction over whether the payment
  has happened yet**, and it is **IDEMPOTENT under bfree**, so there is "no
  data-dependent case split on which free happened to be the first".
* **writei**: naive per-iteration sum gives `wi_cost 1023 FW_MAX = 25` vs 10 —
  "filewrite's own four-block chunk would be unpayable and the KERNEL would be
  at fault rather than the proof".  The honest figure is
  `wi_cost_bmonly = 2B + 2`, **exactly 10 at B = 4, with ZERO slack**
  (`WriteiBudget.wi_cost_bmonly_no_slack`).  Two absorptions are modelled (the
  single bitmap block; a freshly ballocated data block, already logged by
  bzero); a third (the indirect block across iterations) is **true and
  deliberately NOT modelled**, parked in `WriteiBudget`'s `LogAmort` section.
* **writei takes NO credit parameter**: its loop invariant carries the unpaid
  bitmap block as one unit of held-back POTENTIAL (`bm_pot`) rather than as a
  case split.
* **dirlink**: a constant budget of 7 is "not a bound create can meet" (create's
  mkdir chain runs its 2nd and 3rd dirlinks with SIX and FIVE units), so the
  set-form contract takes `dl_need crb ind` instead.
* **`ProofWritei.v:4799` records a non-monotonicity trap**: `wi_cost_bmonly 0 0 = 2`
  where the old `wi_cost 0 0` was 1 — the empty range still has a positive
  budget premise.
* **fsinit's off-by-one is a real composition fact**: initlog takes 34 bslots
  and returns only 2 (32 are sealed into `log_state`'s pool **forever**), but
  ireclaim needs 3, so fsinit enters with 35 and holds ONE back across the
  `jal initlog`.

### T6. The bitmap and the inode region are persistent INVARIANTS, not threaded resources

`claude-notes/design/fs-bitmap.md` §"Who owns `bitmap_res` between calls" is
cited in four headers.  Nothing in balloc/bfree/bmap/itrunc holds `bitmap_res`;
it lives in a persistent Iris invariant at an EXISTENTIAL set, and the contracts
**say nothing about which bits are set**.  The ghost move rides **inside
log_write's own atomic update**:

* `BitmapInv.bitmap_alloc_au` supplied to `SpecLogWrite.wp_log_write_au` at
  `Efs := ⊤ ∖ ↑bitmapN` — withdraws the client half, re-parks at `used ∪ {bi}`,
  and pays out the block's `free_blk` **in the same opening**.
* `BitmapInv.bitmap_free_au` is the mirror; "The receipt is `emp`."
* `InodeRegion.ireg_claim_au` — ialloc's claim, "an atomic update with **NO
  resource premise at all**", `Φfsb := True`.
* `InodeRegion.ireg_write_au` — iupdate's.

The *reason* the region owns the halves (`SpecIupdate.v`, fs-icache.md §11.3/§12):

> `fs_chalf` is per BLOCK and a dinode block holds SIXTEEN inodes, so a contract
> that takes the block's half for the duration of the call is **unsatisfiable by
> two lock holders in the same block**.

And what serialises two concurrent `ialloc`s is **the buffer**, not any lock
(`SpecIalloc.v` §16.2): ialloc holds neither the itable spinlock nor any
sleeplock at its `log_write`, "so no caller could hand it the fragment and no
caller could take it back".

### T7. Buffer pinning: the machinery half / client half coupling

The load-bearing lemma of the whole file-system layer, restated per function:

* `bm_held_content` (bmap) — "the load-bearing coupling of the indirect arm: it
  is what makes the word the code reads out of the buffer BE the entry list's
  entry `q`".
* `rd_held_content` (readi), `wi_held_content` (writei), `iu_held_L` (iupdate),
  `BioFs.bio_held_fs_L` + `InodeRegion.ireg_read` (ilock, ialloc, iupdate),
  `BitmapInv.bitmap_read` / `bitmap_read_own` (balloc, bfree).

In each case: the bio handle carries the **machinery** half; the model (region /
`inode_blocks` / bitmap invariant) carries the **client** half; joining them for
one mask-preserving opening pins the buffer's raw bytes to the pure model.  The
existential learned in that window (`used`, `ds`, `data fbn`, `e`) **must not
escape it** — `ProofBalloc.v` spells this out: the `used` binder "exists only
between the bread at `+0xa8` and the log_write at `+0x42`", and every lemma
outside that window "names no set at all".

**Buffer SLOT accounting** is a second, separate ledger (`bslots`): "TWO SLOT
UNITS, in and back out: bread's reference is held across log_write, which wants
one of its own; brelse gives it back" (bfree, iupdate).  `ireclaim` has a
sharper case — **the buffer is held across `iget`** (`+0x44` runs while bread's
reference from `+0x8c` is outstanding; brelse at `+0x4c` only returns it
afterwards).

### T8. Freshness / injectivity: exclusive byte runs are the only proof device

Three distinct obligations all discharge the same way:

* **bfree's dead panic**: two owners of one block's bytes is `False`
  (`FsStateBitmap.free_pool_used`).
* **bmap's three installs** must re-establish `blkmap_wf`'s injectivity, and
  "the ONLY thing that can is balloc's exclusive byte run against the runs
  inside `inode_map` / `inode_blocks`" (`InodeInv.inode_fresh`,
  `FsBlocks.fsblock_ne`).  **`fs_chalf` is a HALF element and two at one key are
  consistent** — so the half alone proves nothing.
* `InodeRegion.dinode_at_excl` in iget's scan/pool argument.

Related: **the fresh block is DEPOSITED, not returned** (bmap takes the caller's
`inode_blocks` bundle and gives it back with the new block in it), so the two
arms are not asymmetric.

### T9. Register / frame budgets: lazily and conditionally saved callee-saved registers

gcc saves some callee-saved registers only on the paths that need them, and the
early exits skip the matching restores.  One `callee_saved` transport does not
fit the whole function, and the headers make this a first-class design concern:

* **bmap, "THE s4 QUIRK"** — `c.sdsp s4,0(sp)` only on the paths reaching bread
  (`+0x058`/`+0x060`), popped once at `+0x088`; the direct path jumps to the
  shared epilogue `+0x08a` **never having touched it**.  So `callee_saved` is
  established **per-arm**, the join is reached with s4 "either restored or never
  written", the epilogue's premise is `bm_thr5` + frame slot 6 held as an
  **ANONYMOUS word** (`bm_frame`), and only the interior lemmas carry `bm_thr6`.
  "That is a fact about bmap's PROOF; the contract below just says
  `callee_saved m mf`."
* **itrunc** — `sd s4,0(sp)` at `+0x50` / `ld s4,0(sp)` at `+0x90`, both INSIDE
  the indirect arm, "so the direct-only path owns the sixth frame slot without
  ever giving it a value.  `it_frame`'s sixth conjunct is **existential** for
  exactly that reason."
* **dirlink** — s1 lazily at `+0x1c`, s3/s4 at `+0x24`/`+0x26`; **FOUR** register
  bundles (`dl_eregs`, `dl_pregs`, `dl_regs`, `dl_tregs`), "each excluding
  exactly the registers that are live-but-unsaved at that point".
* **readi** — the opposite extreme: EVERY callee-saved register is saved (ra +
  s0..s11, 14-slot frame), "so there is no register-threading invariant at all";
  what replaces it is the frame in three strengths (`rd_fr7`/`rd_fr8`/`rd_fr13`).
  "bmap's s4 lesson applies verbatim: every restore precedes the join at `+0xd8`."
* **iunlockput** — a 32-byte frame with only THREE slots used; "the word at sp+0
  is padding gcc never touches, so it rides through as an anonymous `stack_own`
  slot".
* **namex** — s2 and s10 are deliberately OUT of `nx_regs` because they are
  written inside every iteration.

**Frame-carving of C locals out of `stack_own`** is a recurring ghost move:
`namei`'s `name[14]` IS the low two slots of its own 4-slot frame
(`StackBytes.slot_bytes_own`), `dirlookup`'s `de` is two frame slots
(`dlk_slots_bytes` / `dlk_bytes_slots`), `dirlink`'s `de` is at `s0-80`.
`ProofNameiRoot.v` notes the root corner does ONE ghost step FEWER because no
memmove runs and the two slots stay ordinary stack slots.

### T10. gcc codegen quirks the proof has to model

* **The CFG is NOT address order** (`ProofNamex.v` prints an execution-order
  listing precisely because "gcc reordered the blocks").
* **A block gcc emitted TWICE** — readi's five-pop exit at `+0xb2` and `+0xbe`
  is ONE lemma `rd_exit` **parameterised by its PCs**, per
  `claude-notes/durable-notes.md`'s "a code block gcc emitted twice" recipe.
  A third copy at `+0xce..+0xd6` is unreachable and never proved.
* **A second RETURN SITE before the frame push** — ireclaim's `c.jr ra` at
  `+0xc6`, reached from `+0x0a`, returns "with THE FRAME NEVER PUSHED".
* **The loop entered in the MIDDLE** — ireclaim's `c.j +70` at `+0x36` jumps
  past the STEP block to the BODY, so "an invariant stated at the body's top is
  arrived at twice with different histories"; the induction is stated at the
  BODY and the step block takes the wand as a HYPOTHESIS.
* **Dead blocks gcc emitted** — namex `+0xf8..+0x102` re-loads and re-tests a
  byte already decided; the `len = 0` block at `+0x116` is never entered.
* **A duplicated arm rather than a branch** — namex's `L_nlink` is "a FRESH
  BLOCK, not a share of `L_notdir`: gcc emitted a second copy of
  `iunlockput(ip); return 0` rather than branching into the one at `+0x54`,
  because `+0x54` FALLS THROUGH into the return and a branch from `+0xd2` would
  have to jump."
* **Branchless return** — dirlink `+0x90..+0x96`:
  `addi a0,a0,-16; sltu a0,zero,a0; subw a0,zero,a0`, i.e. `a0 = -(writei(...) != 16)`.
* **`c.addi` vs `c.addi16sp`** — nameiparent's pop "is a plain `c.addi sp,sp,16`,
  NOT a `c.addi16sp`: 16 fits the 6-bit signed field, so gcc emits the cheaper
  form.  Hence `wp_caddi_sp_pop_s_sconf` here where a 32-byte frame would want
  `wp_caddi16sp_pop_s_sconf`."  fsinit likewise uses the plain `stk_push_32`
  family, "not the `c.addi16sp` family every deeper fs function uses".
* **Inlining** — `bzero` is inlined inside balloc (`+0x4c`: bread/memset/
  log_write/brelse); `readsb` is inlined inside fsinit ("there is no
  `jal readsb`"); `skipelem` is inlined inside namex ("there is no `skipelem`
  symbol in the image").
* **memset comes in two flavours** — ialloc and balloc link against the
  whole-function `MemsetArray`, "not the `MEMSET_PARTS` module `Memset`".

### T11. Byte encoding, widths, and sign/zero extension

* **Geometry is VERIFIED OFF THE DECODE, not off `fs.c`.**  `SpecDirlookup.v`:
  "172 bytes.  Geometry VERIFIED off CodeDirlookup.v, not off fs.c".
  `SpecDirlink.v` checks that the callee at `+0x78` is **`strncpy` (0x80000dd6),
  not safestrcpy**.  `SpecNamecmp.v` verifies `DIRSIZ` off the image
  (`li a2,14`).
* **`lhu` vs `lh`** — dirlookup's free test is "the ZERO-EXTENDING
  `lhu a5,-96(s0)` … so it is the halfword and not a byte"; iget's arguments are
  `lw a0,0(s2)` (SIGN-extended) and `lhu a1,-96(s0)` (ZERO-extended).
* **`stati`'s one observable extension** — four of the five load/store pairs are
  same-width so the extension is undone by the store's truncation; the fifth
  (`lwu a5,76(a0)` then `sd a5,16(a1)`) widens, so `st->size` is the
  ZERO-extension.  "That is the one place a mis-read of the flag would have
  produced a false contract".  And: "The AST's boolean is `is_unsigned`, so
  `false` is lh/lw and `true` is lhu/lwu -- **easy to read backwards**."
* **32-bit ARGUMENTS ARRIVE SIGN-EXTENDED**, uints included, so a `uint` ≥ 2^31
  "arrives in a3/a4 as a NEGATIVE 64-bit word" (`SpecReadi.v`, and the NOTE at
  `ProofReadiParts.v:201`).  What this costs is "one reading of the
  `bltu a5,a3` at `+0x002`: a sign-extended-negative a3 is ABOVE the size as an
  unsigned 64-bit word, which is what makes that 64-bit compare decide the
  32-bit unsigned one the C is written in."
* **Scalings** — bmap's byte offsets are `slli 0x20 / srli 0x1e` (zero-extend
  then ×4); bfree's `bi` is `(b << 51) >> 54`; balloc's `bi/8` is a SIGNED divide
  via `sraiw`.
* **`lia` cannot see through `bv_unsigned`** — `ProofBmapParts.v`: "the
  arithmetic behind it is factored into an `mword`-free helper over plain `Z`,
  because `lia` answers 'Cannot find witness' as soon as a `bv_unsigned` is in
  the goal (claude-notes/durable-notes.md)."  **Port this verbatim to Lean:
  factor `omega`-shaped goals into `Int`/`Nat`-only helpers.**
* **The name model** — `DirentEnc.bname n f` is the prefix before the first NUL
  capped at n; `nc_zero_iff` "needs NO padding or well-formedness hypothesis on
  either side"; strncpy NUL-pads, so the stored record IS `de_of_name`; namex's
  LONG branch copies 14 bytes with **NO terminator**.
* **`DirentEnc.v:100`**: "every law below is stated with the LITERALS 14 / 16 /
  64, never with these names."
* **Little-endian word decoding** — fsinit's `fsi_img` reads the superblock image
  as eight LE words and it "is literally `BlockWords.ind_bytes` at an eight-entry
  list"; `ByteBuf.bb_chunk` regroups the 32-byte window; `fsi_word4` folds each
  record into the `↦₄` cell.  Four of the eight addresses match `BitmapInv.v` /
  `InodeInv.v` **by `reflexivity`**.

### T12. Iris proof-mode PERFORMANCE — stated as a hard requirement, not style

`ProofNamex.v` is explicit and quantitative:

> the BODY of every one of them is a named `nx_*_body` Definition above the
> capstone rather than spelled out at the `iAssert`.  That is a **performance
> requirement, not a style choice**: nine of these statements are live at the
> deepest point, the proof term is the Iris context times the number of steps it
> survives, and naming them was **5:36 -> 3:48 and 118M -> 69M tree nodes**.
> They must stay **TRANSPARENT (never `Typeclasses Opaque`)** or the `iApply`s
> below stop unifying -- see claude-notes/optimization.md, "RULE ONE".

Related structural rules, repeated across the cone:

* **A `Proof*.v` file may not `Require` another `Proof*.v` file.**
  `ProofNamexParts.v`: "A `Require` between two Proof*.v files is pure critical
  path (claude-notes/optimization.md, 'Build shape')."  Consequence: pure lemmas
  wanted by two proofs are **re-derived** in each `*Parts.v`
  (`ProofReadiParts.v`, `ProofWriteiParts.v` both say so).
* **`*Parts.v` exists so the whole-function file re-checks without re-checking
  the pure layer** (`ProofDirlookupParts.v`, `ProofBmapParts.v`,
  `ProofItruncParts.v`, `ProofNamexParts.v`).
* **`Spec*.v` requires only the definitional layer, never a whole-function proof
  file, "so every function proof can be checked in parallel"** — the opening
  sentence of a dozen Spec headers.  And: "a Spec file must not require another
  function's Spec" (`SpecFsinit.v`, which is why `ROOTDEV` was hoisted into
  `InodeInv.v`).
* **Ambient PERSISTENT resources are introduced with `#`** — `ProofDirlookup.v`:
  the nine ambient resources "are all PERSISTENT and are introduced with `#` …
  it is what keeps the loop's universal down to the genuinely linear ones."
* **Leaf lemmas were parked in `*Parts.v` only because editing the shared file
  invalidated the downstream `.vo` tree** — `ProofBallocParts.v`,
  `ProofBfree.v`: they have since moved to `WpSconfAlu.v`.  A Lean port should
  put them in the shared ALU file from the start.
* **`ProofWritei.v:2342`**: "`destruct ... eqn:` SUBSTITUTES the scrutinee, so
  `Hbc1`/`Hbc5` carry the literal `true`/`false` from here on -- the arm facts
  must be named at the literal, not at `bmap_alloced bmI bm2 fbn`."  And: "the
  step lemmas conclude at `S W - 1`, which unification does NOT reduce to `W` on
  its own."

### T13. Loop-invariant SHAPES: fuel induction, and which shape to pick

Three distinct shapes, and the choice is forced by whether the body sleeps:

1. **Ordinary Coq fuel induction** on a `nat` measure — `ProofIinit.v` says why
   *not* iLöb: "proved -- like freerange's loop over kfree -- by ordinary Coq
   fuel induction on the number of inodes left, **NOT iLoeb (the packaged sconf
   leaves strip the step's later, so a later-guarded IH could never be
   applied)**."
2. **The loop entirely inside a critical section** — `ProofIget.v`: "the whole
   loop sits INSIDE the critical section, so `b = false` and every leaf collapses
   through `wp_next_off_intro` with NO hart threading at all.  The entry hart
   does not have to ride the induction's universal."  Also: `M` and `ci` are
   FIXED across the scan, so the big-op threads through unchanged.
3. **`ProofKexit`'s `∀ fuel, wp_next` shape** — required when the body sleeps:
   `ProofDirlookup.v`: "dirlookup's body SLEEPS inside readi, so the hart moves
   at every call and **the loop statement has to quantify its own `CpuId`**."
   Same for dirlink's `Hloop` and namex's `Hloop` (which nests three more loops
   of the same shape).

Measures actually used: `Z.to_nat (BPB - bi)` (balloc), `Z.to_nat (ninodes - inum)`
(ialloc, ireclaim), the straddled-block count (readi `rd_blocks_step`, writei
`wi_blocks_step`), `plen - off` (namex), `NINODE - cursor` (iget).

Invariant-shape choices worth copying:
* **itrunc's direct loop** state is `replicate k 0 ++ drop k (bm_dir bm)`
  "rather than as an iterated `<[i := 0]>` because the two ends … are then both
  **definitional**, and the step is one `insert_take_drop` rewrite."
* **itrunc's two loops get DIFFERENT invariants**: the direct loop clears each
  cell it frees; the indirect loop "does NOT clear them … Its state is therefore
  not a changing map at all … **That asymmetry is why the two loops get
  different invariants rather than one parameterised one.**"
* **Both loops free into the persistent invariant**, so "no partial sum is
  carried and no assembly arithmetic exists: the `bm_dir_freed`/`bm_ent_freed`/
  `bm_blocks_split` vocabulary this file used to define **died** with the
  threaded bitmap."

### T14. Joins: prove the shared tail ONCE, with an ABSTRACT continuation

Every multi-exit function does this, and it is the main structuring device:

* `ProofDirlookup.v`'s `Htail` — a persistent `wp_next`-wrapped assertion at
  `+0x96` "with a CONTINUATION `∀ mf, callee_saved m mf → mf!!!a0 = Mt!!!a0 → …`;
  each of the three arms that reach it supplies its own continuation carrying its
  own linear resources.  **Stating it that way is what keeps the arm payloads out
  of the tail.**"
* `ProofDirlink.v`'s `Htail` (2 arms) and `Hafter` (3 arms) — and the note that
  `Hafter` **cannot** hold an abstract continuation because strncpy/`sh`/writei
  live in it.
* `ProofNamex.v`'s `Htail` — FOUR arms, "so it must speak only about the twelve
  frame slots and `nx_tregs`".
* `ProofIput.v`'s `ip_tail` — FOUR entries, three on the ENTRY hart and one
  after four parking calls, so it is "anchored at the function's entry hart in
  `ProofAcquiresleep.asl_exit`'s style -- its own ambient `CID` is a fresh
  binder, the caller's continuation is a `wp_next (CID0 := CID0)` premise, and
  the chained equality comes in as `Hanch`.  **Nothing else in the file needs
  that.**"
* `ProofIget.v` proves the tail **BEFORE the loop**, as the loop's own last
  `-∗`: "Proving it early is what keeps the six stack cells out of the
  induction: the tail already owns them."

And the converse — **one block reached from TWO places** — `ProofNamex.v`'s
`Hrest` and `Hdlblk`, "stated ONCE as a nested `iAssert` that CONSUMES the
induction hypothesis and the contract's continuation…  Without them the whole
ilock / type-test / dirlookup / four-exit tail would have to be transcribed
twice, and the dirlookup block four times."

**And the two-exit resource-splitting trick** (`ProofNamex.v`): "`Hmid` and
`Hhead` each take TWO spatial continuations, and the walk's thirty-slot bundle
cannot be split between them.  The way out is to **DECIDE THE ARM ON THE DATA
first** … give the whole bundle to the arm that actually runs, and REFUTE the
other one from its own exit facts."

### T15. Sleeping, parking, `eb`, and `noff`

A uniform boilerplate paragraph ends almost every Spec header:

> X SLEEPS (bread, …), so it threads the full running-process bundle exactly as
> SpecBread.v does: `procs_inv` / `p_pid`, the disk fabric (`dev_inv` /
> `disk_geom` / the virtio_disk lock), and the trap-CSR complement
> (`trap_csrs_ext eb` / `cpu_claim_ext eb pj`, index-free).  It enters and
> returns at **noff 0**.

Exceptions to memorise: `stati`, `namecmp`, `iinit`, `idup`, `iget`, `iunlock`
do **not** sleep (iunlock still threads `procs_inv` because releasesleep WAKES
sleepers, "exactly as SpecBrelse.v does for the same call").  `balloc` "enters
and returns at noff 0 but **PARKS internally**, so its own crossing is the
literal `true`, not `b`."  `iput`'s bundle is **UNCONDITIONAL** — "xv6's iput
always MAY truncate and no caller can know in advance which arm runs."

The hard blocker and its resolution (`SpecIput.v` B1) is worth porting verbatim:

> iput calls acquiresleep at noff = 1 (itable.lock held), and the blocking
> `SpecAcquiresleep` demands `cpu_own 0 ...`.  SETTLED … the truncate arm calls
> `wp_acquiresleep_nb_sconf`, the NON-BLOCKING contract, which never reaches the
> sleeping branch at all -- **REF-1 says no share of the entry's "may hold" right
> exists, so nobody holds the lock**.  The earlier plan leaned on the sleeping
> branch being `panic("sched locks")`; that contract is gone, because **nothing
> that CAN sleep may be entered at noff != 0.**

`ProofIput.v` adds the `b` discipline: "`b` is pinned `true`… Prologue and
epilogue are hart-generic at `b`; the whole body between the two `acquire`s runs
at the literal `false` and collapses through `wp_next_off_intro`; the stretch
between the release at `+0x5c` and the re-acquire at `+0x82` is back at `b` and
is the only place a hart moves."

`ProofIinit.v:52` is the per-lemma `CpuId` binder rule (see 6.0b).

### T16. Premises that were REMOVED because they were UNSUPPLIABLE or UNPRESERVABLE

The most transferable methodological lesson in the cone.  Four cases:

1. **The granularity premise `16 | di_size dn`** (dirlookup and dirlink).
   "It is **NOT an invariant**", and "**dirlink's OWN short-write arm is what
   breaks it**".  Removing it made two panics LIVE, and
   `SpecDirlink.v` states the behavioural consequence bluntly:
   "A dirlink on a directory a previous short write corrupted therefore PANICS
   rather than returning; that is what the C does, and it is the honest
   post-state."
2. **dirlink's `size + 16 <= MAXFILE*BSIZE`** — "It was **UNSUPPLIABLE**: it is
   a fact about `dp`, the record nameiparent finds at RUN TIME, which no
   caller's contract has a word for -- and **dirlink itself destroys the
   proposition by growing the directory, so it is not even preservable.**"
3. **v1's `i_ref ip ↦₄{dqr} refv` premise and the `inode_key` shadow** — both
   "UNSATISFIABLE" / "unsatisfiable for the second holder": with N reference
   holders only two `ghost_var` halves exist.  `SpecIdup.v` records the same
   trap in its old postcondition: "it returned `cwd_ref ip ∗ cwd_ref ip`, i.e.
   **fraction 1 twice, which is satisfiable only while the predicate is `emp`**."
4. **`SpecNamex.v`'s old `p_cwd pj ↦₈{dqc} cwdv` row** — "which is the whole cell
   twice over, and so was **uncallable**"; the fix is to BORROW the cell out of
   `proc_priv_bare` for the one load and hand it back.

Compare `SpecWritei.v`'s explicit reasoning about **why two facts are stated as
PRESERVATIONS rather than as facts**: neither the size cap nor `inode_sized` is
provable outright, "So both would have to be PREMISES, at which point they would
ripple into SpecDirlink and every caller below it.  Stating the implication
instead costs a re-parking caller nothing."

### T17. IMAGE / BOOT-CLIENT premises: threaded, never discharged — "an axiom would be a lie"

`SpecFsinit.v` is the home of this and says it best:

> They are stated here as premises ABOUT THE IMAGE'S BLOCK 1 … and they are
> **THREADED, not discharged**.  That is the honest shape and it is deliberate:
> they are claims about what mkfs wrote … **The boot client supplies them; no
> function proof can, and an axiom would be a lie.**

The five IOUs: `1 < ninodes`, `ninodes <= 16 * nib`, `ninodes < 2^31`,
`icfg_dev = ROOTDEV`, `0 < icfg_nib` — plus `sb_magic = FSMAGIC`.  The same
family includes `IcacheBoot.ipool_alloc`'s allocated-inum bundles,
`InodeLock.inode_ok`, and `DirView.dir_ok`.

`SpecFsinit.v` also explains **why the superblock has no abstraction**: before
`+0x26` `&sb` is 32 bytes of raw .bss; "this contract is the only place in the
tree where a fact about the superblock can be stated as a fact about anything at
all."  And the log gnames are **BAKED at `icfg_log`** here rather than
existential: "An existential `∃ γ` could never be shown equal to the ambient
field … a tie carried in a body existential admits no agreement with a
consumer's γ."

### T18. The icache reference algebra — the deepest set of traps

* **`positiveR` has no zero**, so **a SHARE carries no count fragment** and
  **a share cannot BECOME a reference**.  `SpecIdup.v`: "Under `natR` a share IS
  authority mass … Under `positiveR` the identity budget forbids it … A share
  therefore cannot BECOME a reference."  Consequence: every `ref < 1` guard reads
  through the **LIVENESS SLICE** instead of a count fragment
  (`iref_live_load_au`), and that lemma "takes `k < NINODE` as a premise where
  its count-side twin derived it from `icM_wf`".
* **The carve / gather discipline**: `inode_ref_shed` (or `inode_ref_carve`)
  splits a reference into a share for ilock plus an `inode_ref_short` parent;
  `inode_ref_gather` re-forms it.  `iunlockput` exists exactly to do the gather
  **between its two calls**, because "iunlock returns a SHARE … iput spends a
  canonical REFERENCE … the two do NOT compose on their own".
* **The two-parkers problem** (`SpecIunlock.v` §14.8): iput's window-exit parker
  holds an otherwise identical bundle, so the checkout **DESCRIPTOR**
  (`IcacheEscrow.ic_deposit`) is a PREMISE, "and it is not bookkeeping: it is
  what tells this parker's arm from iput's".
* **PARKED-MEANS-FLUSHED** — "park only with the region record retagged to the
  record you are parking".  Without it "iget's eviction could never conclude the
  pool's allocated shape … from the parked arm's".  "Stale in-memory records
  exist only INSIDE a critical section, between a writei and its iupdate."
* **`iref_slot`, a unit of a FIXED supply, is what proves the incremented count
  is still an `int`** — "`ip->ref++` is unconditional, so it cannot re-establish
  'the count is still an int' on its own -- the missing step is **false at
  2^31 - 1 and no axiom may assert it**."
* **iget's pair-vs-inum mismatch (§13.11)** — "the dev compare at `+0x4c`
  **short-circuits** to the loop step BEFORE `ip->inum` is ever loaded, so a scan
  that misses proves only that no live slot carries THE PAIR -- while the pool,
  the region and `dinode_at` are keyed on the inum ALONE."  Fixed by making
  `is_itable2` carry the table's device (single-device cache).
* **iput's WINDOW (§13.13)** — "iput reads `ip->valid` at `+0x3c` holding only
  itable.lock, and **CANNOT use the answer at the checkout twenty bytes later**:
  `ic_open_auth_ref` re-seals the parked arm with its polarity existentially
  bound."  The fix: don't re-seal at PARKED at all; close at `ic_held`, taking
  the PAYLOAD out at the polarity just observed — "A resource in this proof's own
  context is not re-bound by anything."  The window's credential is **REF-1
  rather than the checkout token**, because the `+0x44` exit must undo it with no
  `acquiresleep` having run.
* **iget's recycle does NO eviction and NO `ipool_put`** — "under §13.9 a
  recycled slot is not live, so its arm is EMPTY … that is iput's job".
* **The claim box** — ialloc's retagged fragment STAYS in the region at
  `fresh_shape`; `NLINK STAYS 0` until the caller's own iupdate; ilock's
  postcondition exposes it as a **conditional** `filled : bool`, and it HAS to be
  conditional because `fresh_shape dn` is FALSE on the other two arms.
* **`ProofIdup.v`'s atomicity argument** — the `ref` word lives in
  `itable_inv`, not in any lock's resource ("it has to, because ilock and
  iunlock read it holding no lock at all"), so both memory steps are
  atomic-update leaves; what makes the read-modify-write atomic *in the proof* is
  that idup holds itable.lock across all three instructions and the lock holds
  HALF the authority.

### T19. Postconditions: exactness, and what is deliberately NOT claimed

* **writei's DISTURBED REGION** (kernel defect D1's fix): on a part-way
  `either_copyin` failure writei now COMMITS the partial chunk, so the file
  genuinely changes OUTSIDE `[off, off+tot)`.  The post admits `dist ≤ BSIZE`
  unspecified bytes at `off+tot`, with `dist = 0` when no copy failed **and** the
  third clause `user = false → dist = 0` (provable because the kernel path is a
  memmove with no fault to take).  Without the tightening, "the write could have
  clobbered up to 64 FOLLOWING records with arbitrary bytes and dir-wf was
  underivable".
* **readi needs NO existential** — `rd_delivered` "is exact on both ends", where
  writei needed an existential `wrote` because its source was user memory.
* **readi's return value is TWO arms, not three** — the up-front bounds failure
  "IS the second arm with `tot = 0`", and collapsing them "is what makes the
  contract exact rather than merely bounded".
* **On a faulting user copy, `tot` is the loop counter PLUS whatever the failing
  chunk managed** — "that is why the -1 arm's `tot` is not the loop counter".
* **A SHORT WRITE IS A NORMAL RETURN** — "A contract promising `tot = n` would be
  unprovable and one treating a short write as failure would be useless to
  filewrite."  And the writing arm must also REPORT the EOF guard it passed, or
  "the contract PERMITS a success past the end of the file, which the code cannot
  produce … its delta is WRONG rather than merely unprovable."
* **stati leaves bytes 12..15 unmentioned** — "they are the alignment hole …
  saying anything about them here would be a claim stati does not make."
* **namex makes NO path → inode functional claim** — "each dirlookup is atomic
  under its own directory's lock and **no stable global tree exists between
  iterations under concurrency**, so the honest refinement would be a ghost
  trace … which earns nothing at this altitude."  Only the locally-produced
  name-buffer clause is functional.
* **iget's two arms are INDISTINGUISHABLE and must be** — "xv6's whole point is
  that a second `iget` of a cached inode is indistinguishable from the first."
* **bmap's failure arm does NOT claim `bm' = bm`** — "the indirect-path failure
  can already have allocated and installed the INDIRECT block before failing on
  the data block, so 'the map is unchanged' would simply be false there."
* **ialloc's `ialloc_fresh` "says nothing about the region's state at RETURN
  time -- by then another hart may already have locked the new inode."**
* **`blk_holes_zero`**: without normalising unallocated indices "the clause above
  is **false the moment writei extends the file**".

### T20. Contract multiplicity: one function, several contracts

Do not assume one C function ⇒ one Lean theorem.  The tree carries:

* `wp_X_sconf` (the set-forgetting / counted form) **and** `wp_X_gen` (the
  credited / set form) for balloc, bmap, bfree, dirlink, iput, ialloc, itrunc,
  iupdate, namex, nameiparent, namei, writei.  "The counted form is DERIVED from
  it -- `log_op` IS `∃ Sb, log_opS` -- so no existing caller moves."
* `BMAP_NOALLOC` (`wp_bmap_noalloc_sconf`) — a second bmap contract.
* **ROOT CORNERS**: `wp_namex_root` / `wp_namei_root`, whose proofs take ONE
  functor argument (`IGET`) and "touch no resource but the inode cache and the
  two path bytes.  Everything the walk needs and this does not -- the log, the
  bio cache, the inode region, the bitmap, the disk lock, the running process --
  is absent from the statement, which is the whole point of the corner."
* **ERA contracts** (`SpecNameiEra`, `SpecNamexEra`) — deliberate COPY-ADAPT
  duplicates of the frozen trace contracts with ONE resource changed at the hop.
  "COPY-ADAPT IS THE RULED APPROACH … and it is **TRANSITIONAL BY DESIGN** …
  Until then the two contracts stand side by side and **the diff IS the
  review**."  `ProofNamexEra.v` lists its own diff "EXHAUSTIVELY (there is
  nothing else to look for)".
* `wp_iunlockput_dep_gen` / `_tx_sconf` / `_tx_gen`, `wp_ilock_dep_sconf` /
  `_tx_sconf`, `wp_iupdate_{sconf,gen,cred,credgen,link,unlink}` — dependency vs
  transaction forms, and link/unlink specialisations.

Also: **dirlookup BORROWS three things and returns them verbatim on both arms**
(`dlinks`, `dinode_at` for the HOME record, and the `IgetLic.iname` licence),
"which is why the borrow costs the six call sites nothing but a `iFrame`".  The
licence is **returned at the SAME `l`** — "a `∃ l'` post is equally sound and
silently permits a licence swap, which would destroy the per-site documentation
the increment exists for."  And a pure premise is a **DISJUNCTION, and that is
forced**, because "a bare 'the home's count is nonzero' premise is UNSUPPLIABLE
at sys_unlink".

### balloc

#### `iris/SpecBalloc.v`  (415 lines)

**(a) Header block — lines 1-89, verbatim:**

```coq
(* SpecBalloc.v -- the public interface of balloc, stated independently of
   any proof.  balloc IS PROVEN: [ProofBalloc.v]'s [BallocProof] functor is
   the single instance of the [Module Type] below, and [LinkBalloc.v]
   carries no [Axiom].  A NEW [Parameter] HERE IS THEREFORE A PROOF
   OBLIGATION ON THAT FUNCTOR, not a free contract widening -- widening this
   interface costs work in a 4100-line proof file.  (It is still not an
   assumption in anyone's [Print Assumptions] cone: a [Module Type]
   parameter discharged by a real proof adds nothing.)

     static uint balloc(uint dev) {
       int b, bi, m;
       struct buf *bp = 0;
       for(b = 0; b < sb.size; b += BPB){
         bp = bread(dev, BBLOCK(b, sb));
         for(bi = 0; bi < BPB && b + bi < sb.size; bi++){
           m = 1 << (bi % 8);
           if((bp->data[bi/8] & m) == 0){    // is the block free?
             bp->data[bi/8] |= m;            // mark it in use
             log_write(bp);
             brelse(bp);
             bzero(dev, b + bi);
             return b + bi;
           }
         }
         brelse(bp);
       }
       printf("balloc: out of blocks\n");
       return 0;
     }

   THE CONTRACT (claude-notes/design/fs-inode.md, "balloc's contract").
   Two arms, on the returned a0:

   - SUCCESS -- a nonzero block b, with the two facts every FS-layer
     consumer of a block number needs ([b] is covered, and it is NOT one of
     the log's own storage blocks), plus b's own [fs_chalf] half at ALL
     ZEROES: bzero has already log_written the block as a zero block, so
     the caller receives a zeroed block and not an arbitrary one.  Spends
     TWO budget units -- the bitmap's log_write plus bzero's.

   - FAILURE -- returns 0, spends nothing, gives nothing: the reservation
     comes back at its full [2 + u].  The arm-dependent budget costs
     nothing to state because the postcondition is already a two-arm
     disjunction on the return value.

   *** THE OUT-OF-BLOCKS ARM IS LIVE, AND IT CALLS printk. ***  Nothing in
   [BitmapInv.bitmap_res] prevents every bit below [sb.size] being set --
   the free pool is then all-[emp] -- so the
   scan CAN fall out of the loop and reach
   [auipc a0,0x4 / addi a0,a0,1350 / jal printk] on "balloc: out of blocks".
   That is the GENERAL printk path ([SpecPrintk.v]), not the panic path,
   so this contract takes:

     - [γpr] and the two PERSISTENT credentials [kernel_data] and
       [printk_env γpr γu γd] (the format string itself needs no premise:
       [KernelDataInv.kernel_data_string_all] mints its persistent string out of
       [kernel_data]);

   THE BITMAP IS AN INVARIANT, NOT A PREMISE.  balloc reads BOTH superblock
   fields out of memory ([sb.size] at sb+4, [sb.bmapstart] at sb+28), so
   the two cells are premises, as plain FRACTIONAL cells the way
   SpecInitlog.v takes [sb + 20].  The bitmap block and its FREE POOL live
   in [BitmapInv.bitmap_inv], a persistent Iris invariant at an
   EXISTENTIAL set: the contract says nothing about which bits are set,
   and the postcondition's byte run comes out of the pool at log_write's
   own ghost step ([BitmapInv.bitmap_alloc_au], the supplier for
   [SpecLogWrite.wp_log_write_au]).  This is [InodeRegion]'s shape,
   one layer over; claude-notes/design/fs-bitmap.md has the argument.

   ONE BITMAP BLOCK, AND A THIRD DEAD ARM.  [FSSIZE = 2000 < BPB = 8192],
   so [0 < size <= BPB] is a premise, BBLOCK collapses
   ([BitmapInv.BBLOCK_single]) and the outer loop runs a single iteration:
   b starts at 0, the inner scan exits on [b + bi >= sb.size] or on
   [bi == BPB], and [b += BPB] then makes [b >= sb.size] unconditionally.
   The [0 < size] half of that premise also kills balloc's OWN
   [beqz a5,+0xf6] at +0x12 -- the [sb.size == 0] jump straight to the
   printk, skipping the s2..s8 restore -- which is dead in the same sense
   as log_write's two panics, bmap's "out of range" and bfree's "freeing
   free block": the premise makes the arm unreachable, so it is refuted
   rather than proved.

   balloc SLEEPS (it breads), so it threads the running-process bundle
   exactly as SpecBread.v does: procs_inv / p_pid, the disk fabric
   (dev_inv / disk_geom / the virtio_disk lock), and the trap-CSR complement
   ([trap_csrs_ext eb] / [cpu_claim_ext eb pj], index-free -- see
   claude-notes/completed/eb-generic-sweep.md) that bread's own contract now
   demands.  It enters and returns at noff 0 but PARKS internally, so its
   own crossing is the literal [true], not [b].  The parked scheduler record
   is not threaded -- it lives in the running proc's own [p->lock]. *)
```

#### `iris/SpecBfree.v`  (373 lines)

**(a) Header block — lines 1-60, verbatim:**

```coq
(* SpecBfree.v -- the public interface of bfree, stated independently of its
   proof.  Requires only the definitional layer -- never a whole-function
   proof file -- so every function proof can be checked in parallel.

     static void bfree(int dev, uint b) {
       struct buf *bp;
       int bi, m;

       bp = bread(dev, BBLOCK(b, sb));
       bi = b % BPB;
       m = 1 << (bi % 8);
       if((bp->data[bi/8] & m) == 0)
         panic("freeing free block");
       bp->data[bi/8] &= ~m;
       log_write(bp);
       brelse(bp);
     }

   108 bytes, 35 instructions, straight-line apart from the one panic arm.
   [bi] is computed as [(b << 51) >> 54], i.e. [(b mod BPB) / 8] fused with
   the byte index; [m] as [1 << (b & 7)]; the clear as [xori -1] + [and].

   THE CONTRACT (claude-notes/design/fs-bitmap.md).  bfree consumes the
   freed block's EXCLUSIVE byte run and returns it to the FREE POOL,
   clearing bit [b] of the bitmap block.  The pool and the bitmap block live
   in the persistent [BitmapInv.bitmap_inv]; the block goes back in at
   log_write's own ghost step ([BitmapInv.bitmap_free_au]), so the contract
   names no bitmap set.

   THE PANIC IS DEAD, and the bitmap invariant is what kills it.  The
   caller arrives holding block [b]'s byte run, which is EXCLUSIVE, while
   the free pool holds the run of every block below [size] whose bit is
   CLEAR.  So if bit [b] were clear there would be two owners of one
   block's bytes, which is absurd ([FsStateBitmap.free_pool_used]).  The bit
   is therefore set,
   [bp->data[bi/8] & m] is nonzero ([BitmapEnc.bm_bit_test]), and the
   branch at +0x3a is not taken.  Refuting this panic is the main thing the
   invariant has to buy; the contract still takes the panic credentials
   because bread's own interior panic arm wants them.

   ONE BITMAP BLOCK.  [FSSIZE = 2000 < BPB = 8192], so [size <= BPB] is a
   premise and [BBLOCK b sb = sb.bmapstart] outright
   ([BitmapInv.BBLOCK_single]).  bfree's [srliw a5,a1,0xd] then contributes
   zero and its [(b << 51) >> 54] is just [b / 8].

   THE BUDGET IS SPEND-EXACTLY: [log_op γ (S u)] in, [log_op γ u] out.
   bfree is straight-line and always executes its one log_write, so unlike
   bmap it can promise this (the spend-at-most form is forced only where a
   path can skip the spend).

   TWO SLOT UNITS, in and back out: bread's reference is held across
   log_write, which wants one of its own; brelse gives it back.

   [sb.bmapstart] rides as a plain FRACTIONAL cell, the way SpecInitlog.v
   takes [sb + 20] and SpecIupdate.v takes [sb + 24].  bfree does NOT read
   [sb.size] (only balloc does), so no [sb_size] cell appears here.

   bfree SLEEPS (bread), so it threads the full running-process bundle
   exactly as SpecIupdate.v / SpecBread.v do.  It enters and returns at
   noff 0. *)
```

```coq
(* ProofBfree.v -- bfree over the SIE-agnostic sconf world.

     static void bfree(int dev, uint b) {
       struct buf *bp;  int bi, m;
       bp = bread(dev, BBLOCK(b, sb));
       bi = b % BPB;  m = 1 << (bi % 8);
       if((bp->data[bi/8] & m) == 0) panic("freeing free block");
       bp->data[bi/8] &= ~m;
       log_write(bp);
       brelse(bp);
     }

   STRAIGHT-LINE apart from the one panic arm, which is DEAD.  Two lemmas,
   entered left to right, so the file's two Qeds stay small:

     [bf_tail]          +0x4a .. +0x5e   log_write, brelse, pop, ret and
                                         the contract.
     [wp_bfree_sconf]   +0x00 .. +0x46   prologue, bread, the bit test, the
                                         clear and the byte store.

   NO BITMAP RESOURCE CROSSES THE CONTRACT (claude-notes/design/fs-bitmap.md
   §"Who owns [bitmap_res] between calls").  The bitmap block and the free
   pool live in the persistent [BitmapInv.bitmap_inv]; bfree takes that and
   names no set.  The proof touches the invariant exactly twice:

     - after bread, [BitmapInv.bitmap_read_own] against the handle's
       MACHINERY half ([BioFs.bio_held_fs_L]) -- the parked run never leaves --
       learns [bs0 = bitmap_bytes used] for some [used], [bitmap_ok] at it,
       and [bi ∈ used];
     - at log_write, [SpecLogWrite.wp_log_write_au] fired with
       [lw_au_lb0 (BitmapInv.bitmap_free_au …)]: the block goes back into
       the pool in the SAME opening that re-parks the bitmap at the image of
       [used ∖ {[bi]}].  The receipt is [emp].

   HOW THE PANIC DIES (the point of the whole exercise).  The caller arrives
   holding block [b]'s EXCLUSIVE byte run, while the free pool holds the run
   of every block below [size] whose bit is CLEAR.  The read above therefore
   gives [b ∈ used] outright ([FsStateBitmap.free_pool_used], inside
   [bitmap_read_own]), and
   [BitmapEnc.bm_bit_test] turns that into
   [bp->data[bi/8] & m = 2^(b mod 8) <> 0]: the [c.beqz] at +0x3a falls
   THROUGH, and the arm at +0x60 is never entered.  Nothing about the panic
   is proved -- it is refuted.  The panic credentials are still threaded because
   bread's own interior panic arm wants one.

   ONE BITMAP BLOCK.  [size <= BPB] is a premise, so [BBLOCK b sb] collapses
   to [sb.bmapstart] ([BitmapInv.BBLOCK_single]): the [srliw a5,a1,0xd] at
   +0x0e contributes zero and the [(b << 51) >> 54] at +0x2a/+0x2c is just
   [b / 8].

   THE [sllw] LEAF (the mask [1 << (bi % 8)] at +0x26) LIVES IN

   as [wp_sllw_wval_s_sconf] (the explicit-[wval] reading this file uses)
```

### bmap

#### `iris/SpecBmap.v`  (787 lines)

**(a) Header block — lines 1-87, verbatim:**

```coq
(* SpecBmap.v -- the public interface of bmap, stated independently of its
   proof.  Requires only the definitional layer -- never a whole-function
   proof file -- so every function proof can be checked in parallel.

     static uint bmap(struct inode *ip, uint bn) {
       uint addr, *a;
       struct buf *bp;
       if(bn < NDIRECT){
         if((addr = ip->addrs[bn]) == 0){
           addr = balloc(ip->dev);
           if(addr == 0) return 0;
           ip->addrs[bn] = addr;
         }
         return addr;
       }
       bn -= NDIRECT;
       if(bn < NINDIRECT){
         if((addr = ip->addrs[NDIRECT]) == 0){
           addr = balloc(ip->dev);
           if(addr == 0) return 0;
           ip->addrs[NDIRECT] = addr;
         }
         bp = bread(ip->dev, addr);
         a = (uint * ) bp->data;
         if((addr = a[bn]) == 0){
           addr = balloc(ip->dev);
           if(addr){ a[bn] = addr; log_write(bp); }
         }
         brelse(bp);
         return addr;
       }
       panic("bmap: out of range");
     }

   THE CONTRACT (claude-notes/design/fs-inode.md, "bmap's contract").
   One existential map bm' and the returned block, in two arms:

   - a0 = 0 -- allocation failed, and [blkmap_get bm' bn = 0].  Note that
     bm' is NOT claimed equal to bm: the indirect-path failure can already
     have allocated and installed the INDIRECT block before failing on the
     data block, so "the map is unchanged" would simply be false there.
     What both arms do promise is that bm' agrees with bm at every file
     index except possibly bn.
   - a0 = r <> 0 -- [blkmap_get bm' bn = r].

   Both arms return [inode_map γfs ip bm'] and [blkmap_wf cov logstart bm'].
   The fresh data block is DEPOSITED, not returned: bmap takes the
   caller's [inode_blocks] bundle and gives it back with the freshly
   allocated block in it, so nothing here is asymmetric between the two
   arms (design doc, "Why the fresh block is deposited, not returned").
   The bundles are ALSO what carry each block's EXCLUSIVE byte run, and
   those are what re-establishes [blkmap_wf]'s injectivity when balloc's
   block is installed ([FsBlocks.fsblock_ne]: two owners of one block's
   bytes is [False]).

   THE BUDGET IS SPEND-AT-MOST, not spend-exactly: [log_op γ n] in with
   (5 <= n), and [log_op γ n'] out with (n - 5 <= n' <= n).  bmap cannot
   promise to have spent five, because it has no way to BURN a surplus --
   [log_op] moves only through the ledger authority inside log.lock, which
   bmap never takes -- and on the direct-hit path it does no balloc and no
   log_write at all.  See the clause itself for why the premise is a lower
   bound on the caller's counter rather than a (5 + u) shape.

   THE PANIC ARM IS DEAD.  bmap's [panic("bmap: out of range")] at +0xb2
   is reached only when bn - NDIRECT >= NINDIRECT, which the premise
   (bn < MAXFILE) rules out -- the same way both of log_write's panics are
   dead.  The panic credentials are still threaded, because the interior
   acquire's own holding-check arm wants a panic contract regardless.

   THE s4 QUIRK.  gcc saves s4 only on the paths that reach bread
   ([c.sdsp s4,0(sp)] at +0x058 / +0x060 / +0x0b2) and restores it once at
   +0x088; the direct path jumps straight to the shared epilogue at +0x08a
   and never touches it.  So [callee_saved] is established per-arm rather
   than once at the epilogue -- the join at +0x08a is reached with s4
   either restored or never written.  That is a fact about bmap's PROOF;
   the contract below just says [callee_saved m mf].

   THE BITMAP IS AN INVARIANT, because balloc's is.  bmap takes the two
   superblock cells and the persistent [BitmapInv.bitmap_inv] and says
   nothing about the bitmap on the way out (claude-notes/design/fs-bitmap.md,
   "Who owns bitmap_res between calls").

   [BMAP_NOALLOC] below is UNCHANGED by this: with all three allocation
   sites dead there is no balloc, hence no bitmap and no superblock cell.

   bmap SLEEPS (bread, and balloc), so it threads the full running-process
   bundle exactly as SpecBread.v does.  It enters and returns at noff 0. *)
```

**(c) Further long design-commentary blocks below the header (verbatim):**

```coq
SpecBmap.v:642-675
(* readi calls bmap, and bmap allocates when the slot is zero -- which calls
   log_write.  But fileread does NOT wrap readi in a transaction, so an
   allocating read would hit panic("log_write outside of trans").  It never
   happens because every block below a file's size is allocated
   ([InodeInv.bm_covers] is that statement), and under the single premise

       bv_unsigned (blkmap_get bm fbn) <> 0

   ALL THREE of bmap's allocation sites are dead:

   - the direct slot test at +0x26 and the indirect ENTRY test at +0x80 are
     decided by the premise itself;
   - the indirect-BLOCK test at +0x4c is decided by the premise TOO, and
     that is why this contract needs no second hypothesis about bm_ind:
     [blkmap_wf]'s "no indirect block => no entries" conjunct read backwards
     ([InodeInv.blkmap_wf_ind_nz]) turns "the entry at an indirect index is
     nonzero" into "the indirect block exists".

   So the contract drops EVERYTHING the allocation arms needed:

   - no [log_op] and no budget premise -- bmap performs no [log_write], so
     there is no reservation to spend and none to hand back;
   - no [log_ctx], and hence no [γ : log_names] at all;
   - [bslot] rather than [bslots 3].  The three were bread's one held
     across balloc's two; with balloc dead only bread's own unit remains,
     and brelse returns it.

   ...and the postcondition is correspondingly exact rather than
   existential: the map and the file's data come back UNCHANGED, and a0 is
   [blkmap_get bm fbn].  It is the same 70 instructions and the same proof
   body as [BMAP] -- see ProofBmap.v's [BmapCore], which is parameterised
   by whether the allocation arms are live and is where BOTH contracts come
   from.  Precedent for two contracts over one function: SpecWalk.v's
   [WALK] / [WALK_NOALLOC]. *)
```

```coq
(* ProofBmapParts.v -- bmap's vocabulary: everything its proof needs that is
   NOT a step of its instruction chain, so ProofBmap.v stays about control
   flow.  (The ProofBreadParts.v / ProofWriteHead.v division of labour.)

   Four groups:

   (1) THE TWO SCALINGS.  bmap computes a byte offset twice, both times as
       [slli 0x20 / srli 0x1e] -- zero-extend the 32-bit index, then multiply
       by four.  [bm_slli32_srli30] is that round trip; the arithmetic behind
       it is factored into an [mword]-free helper over plain [Z], because
       [lia] answers "Cannot find witness" as soon as a [bv_unsigned] is in
       the goal (claude-notes/durable-notes.md).

   (2) THE ADDRESSES.  The three [addrs] cells the code forms are already
       covered by [InodeInv.i_addr_indexed] / [i_addr_ndirect]; what is left
       is [bp->data] and the entry slot inside it, plus that slot's
       4-alignment (bcache geometry, as in write_head).

   (3) WORDS INSIDE THE INDIRECT BLOCK.  [InodeInv] carries the indirect
       block's content as [ind_bytes e] for an ENTRY LIST [e]; ByteBuf's
       window algebra carries it as a naming function.  [bm_ent_read] and
       [bm_ent_store] are the two bridges -- read entry [q], and install a
       new entry [q] -- and [bm_buf_word_acc] borrows that word out of the
       [buf_own] the bio handle carries.

   (4) THE HANDLE.  [bm_held_swap] exchanges the traveling bytes inside a
       [bio_held] (the whole of what bmap does to the buffer), and
       [bm_held_content] is the agreement that identifies those bytes with
       the caller's own [fs_chalf] half -- i.e. with [ind_bytes (bm_ent bm)].
       That agreement is the load-bearing coupling of the indirect arm: it
       is what makes the word the code reads out of the buffer BE the entry
       list's entry [q]. *)
```

#### `iris/ProofBmap.v`  (3827 lines)

**(a) Header block — lines 1-66, verbatim:**

```coq
(* ProofBmap.v -- bmap over the SIE-agnostic sconf world.

     static uint bmap(struct inode *ip, uint bn) {
       uint addr, *a;  struct buf *bp;
       if(bn < NDIRECT){
         if((addr = ip->addrs[bn]) == 0){
           addr = balloc(ip->dev);
           if(addr == 0) return 0;
           ip->addrs[bn] = addr; }
         return addr; }
       bn -= NDIRECT;
       if(bn < NINDIRECT){
         if((addr = ip->addrs[NDIRECT]) == 0){
           addr = balloc(ip->dev);
           if(addr == 0) return 0;
           ip->addrs[NDIRECT] = addr; }
         bp = bread(ip->dev, addr);
         a = (uint * ) bp->data;
         if((addr = a[bn]) == 0){
           addr = balloc(ip->dev);
           if(addr){ a[bn] = addr; log_write(bp); } }
         brelse(bp);
         return addr; }
       panic("bmap: out of range");
     }

   THE SHAPE OF THE PROOF.  Five live arms and a dead panic, joining at the
   shared epilogue +0x8a.  Four lemmas, entered strictly left to right:

     [bm_epilogue]      +0x8a .. +0x98   the join: a0 := s1, pop the frame,
                                         ret, and discharge the contract.
     [bm_release]       +0x82 .. +0x88   brelse, restore s4, fall into the
                                         epilogue.  THREE of the five arms
                                         end here (indirect hit, indirect
                                         data-balloc failure, indirect
                                         data-balloc success).
     [bm_indirect_tail] +0x62 .. +0x80   bread, read a[bn], and the
                                         allocate-and-log block +0x9a..+0xb0.
     [wp_bmap_sconf]    +0x00 .. +0x60   prologue, the direct arm, and the
                                         indirect head.

   THE s4 QUIRK is what fixes that division.  gcc pushes s4 only on the
   paths that reach bread ([c.sdsp s4,0(sp)] at +0x058 / +0x060) and pops it
   once at +0x088; the direct arm jumps to +0x08a having never touched it.
   So [bm_epilogue] is reached with s4 ALREADY equal to its entry value on
   every arm -- restored on the indirect ones, never written on the direct
   ones -- and its premise is exactly that ([bm_thr5], which covers s4),
   plus frame slot 6 held as an ANONYMOUS word ([bm_frame]).  Only the
   interior lemmas, where s4 really is live, carry the weaker [bm_thr6].

   THE PANIC ARM AT +0x0b2 IS DEAD: [bltu a5,a4] at +0x044 compares 255
   against bn-NDIRECT, and the contract's [fbn < MAXFILE] bounds that by
   255, so the branch always falls through.  Refuted, not proved.

   THE COUPLING THAT MAKES THE INDIRECT ARM WORK is [bm_held_content]: the
   caller's own [fs_chalf] half for the indirect block (inside [inode_map]'s
   [ind_res]) against the bio handle's machinery half pins the buffer's
   bytes to [ind_bytes (bm_ent bm)] -- so the word the code reads out of
   [bp->data + 4*(bn-12)] IS entry [bn-12] of the pure entry list.

   FRESHNESS.  Each of the three installs has to re-establish
   [blkmap_wf]'s injectivity, and the ONLY thing that can is balloc's
   exclusive byte run against the runs inside [inode_map] /
   [inode_blocks] ([InodeInv.inode_fresh]); [fs_chalf] is a half element and
   two at one key are consistent.  That is also why bmap takes
   [inode_blocks]: the fresh DATA block's half is deposited there. *)
```

### dirlink

#### `iris/SpecDirlink.v`  (1045 lines)

**(a) Header block — lines 1-159, verbatim:**

```coq
(* SpecDirlink.v -- the public interface of dirlink.

     int
     dirlink(struct inode *dp, char *name, uint inum)
     {
       int off;
       struct dirent de;
       struct inode *ip;

       if((ip = dirlookup(dp, name, 0)) != 0){
         iput(ip);
         return -1;
       }
       for(off = 0; off < dp->size; off += sizeof(de)){
         if(readi(dp, 0, (uint64)&de, off, sizeof(de)) != sizeof(de))
           panic("dirlink read");
         if(de.inum == 0)
           break;
       }
       strncpy(de.name, name, DIRSIZ);
       de.inum = inum;
       if(writei(dp, 0, (uint64)&de, off, sizeof(de)) != sizeof(de))
         return -1;
       return 0;
     }

   170 bytes.  Geometry VERIFIED off CodeDirlink.v: [addi sp,sp,-80] /
   [addi s0,sp,80], so [&de = s0-80] ([addi s4,s0,-80] at +0x2a, and the
   [lhu a5,-80(s0)] free test at +0x42, the [sh s6,-80(s0)] inum store at
   +0x7c, the [addi a2,s0,-80] writei source at +0x84) and
   [&de.name = s0-78] ([addi a0,s0,-78] at +0x74, strncpy's destination);
   [li a2,14] at +0x70 is DIRSIZ; the callee at +0x78 is **strncpy**
   (0x80000dd6), not safestrcpy.  THREE registers are saved LAZILY (s1 at
   +0x1c, s3/s4 at +0x24/+0x26) and the two early exits skip their
   restores.

   The return value is computed BRANCHLESSLY at +0x90..+0x96:
   [addi a0,a0,-16; sltu a0,zero,a0; subw a0,zero,a0], i.e.
   [a0 = -(writei(...) != 16)].

   ---- WHY THE CONTRACT IS THE UNION OF THREE ---------------------------

   dirlink is the campaign's widest precondition: it calls dirlookup (hence
   readi, namecmp and iget), iput on the found arm, and readi/strncpy/writei
   on the other.  So it threads dirlookup's bundle, writei's log +
   inode-region + bitmap bundle, and iput's itrunc geometry, all at once.
   It runs INSIDE A TRANSACTION (writei's bmap can allocate).

   TWO PREMISES ARE QUANTIFIED OVER RECORDS RATHER THAN NAMED, because the
   record dirlookup stops at is not known until it stops:

   - [DirView.dir_inums_ok] -- iget's argument bound (see SpecDirlookup.v).
     Since fs-icache.md §15(a) a caller gets it out of the icache: it is
     the conjunct [DirView.dir_ok icfg_nib dn data] riding in
     [IcacheEscrow.ic_loaded];
   - [ireg_blocks_ok] -- iput's [IBLOCK inum inodestart] membership facts,
     stated for EVERY inum the region covers rather than for the one child.
     That is strictly the better shape: it is a fact about the superblock
     layout, provable once, instead of a fact about a directory's contents.

   ---- THE GRANULARITY PREMISE IS GONE (fs-icache.md §15(b)) -----------

   [16 | di_size dn] used to be a premise here too, refuting
   panic("dirlink read") at +0x60 (the [bne a0,s3] at +0x3e).  It is not a
   system invariant -- dirlink's OWN short-write arm is what breaks it (see
   the APPEND arm below: on [tot < 16] the new size is [16*k0 + tot]) -- so
   the short-readi turn is now a LIVE panic arm, discharged with
   [SpecPanic]'s own contract, and no caller owes granularity.  A dirlink on a
   directory a previous short write corrupted therefore PANICS rather than
   returning; that is what the C does, and it is the honest post-state.

   ---- THE ARMS ---------------------------------------------------------

   FOUND (the name is already there): a0 = -1, the directory's data, block
   map and metadata are UNCHANGED, the child reference dirlookup minted has
   been spent by iput ([used' <= used], iput's spend-at-most budget), and
   the ledger unit comes back.

   APPEND: [dir_first data nrec s = None], and writei ran at
   [off = 16 * dir_slot data nrec] -- the first FREE record, or [nrec]
   itself when every record is live, which is where the scan's own [s1]
   lands.  TWO failures answer [a0 = -1 /\ tot < 16]: a SHORT WRITE (bmap
   out of blocks), and writei's OWN -1 return.  The second is the FULL
   DIRECTORY and nothing else -- [off <= size] because the slot is at most
   [nrec], so writei's first reason ([size < off]) is dead, and its second
   ([MAXFILE*BSIZE < off + 16]) forces [off = size = MAXFILE*BSIZE], since
   [off] and [MAXFILE*BSIZE] are both multiples of sixteen and
   [size <= MAXFILE*BSIZE].  It returns with EVERYTHING unchanged at
   [tot = 0], which is what this arm's [tot = 0] corner already says, so it
   needs no arm of its own: [wi_dinode] is the IDENTITY there (the append
   offset is in range, so the size does not move, and the map is the one
   [di_addrs] already names).

   (Until D₀-a this contract carried a premise [size + 16 <= MAXFILE*BSIZE]
   that killed writei's -1 return outright.  It was UNSUPPLIABLE: it is a
   fact about [dp], the record nameiparent finds at RUN TIME, which no
   caller's contract has a word for -- and dirlink itself destroys the
   proposition by growing the directory, so it is not even preservable.  See
   projects/fs-sysfile.md, the eleventh stop.)

   On [tot = 16] the window holds [dirent_bytes (de_of_name inum s)] --
   strncpy NUL-pads, so the stored record IS [DirentEnc.de_of_name] -- and
   the size is raised by writei's own [wi_dinode].

   ---- THE RANGE CLAUSE IS EXACT (fs-icache.md §15.1(i), retrofitted) ----

   writei's postcondition concedes a DISTURBED REGION of up to BSIZE
   unspecified bytes above the written window, because a user copy that
   faults part-way is committed without advancing [tot].  dirlink writes
   from a KERNEL buffer ([user = false]), where either_copyin cannot fail
   at all, and SpecWritei now says so: [user = false -> dist = 0].  So the
   clause below is TWO-way, not three-way, and the third arm -- the SHORT
   write, [tot < 16] -- differs from the old file in exactly the [tot]
   bytes it wrote and NOWHERE ELSE.

   That is what a writer needs to re-park [DirView.dir_ok] over a
   middle-slot link: under the old clause the write could have clobbered
   up to 64 FOLLOWING records with arbitrary bytes and dir-wf was
   underivable (§15.1(i)).  [DirView.dir_ok_dirlink] is the derivation the
   tightened clause unlocks; create (fs-sysfile S5) is its first caller.

   ---- THE LINKED INUM'S RANGE PREMISE ---------------------------------

   [bv_unsigned inum < 16 * nib] on the mword-16 argument is NOT used by
   dirlink's own proof -- the [sh] stores sixteen bits whatever they are.
   It is here for the WRITER: [dir_ok] over the new directory needs every
   live record's inum inside the inode region, and the record dirlink just
   stored carries [inum].  (On a one-byte short write the stored halfword
   is [inum mod 256], which the premise still bounds -- the free slot's
   old high byte is zero.  See [dir_ok_dirlink].)  Stating it now keeps
   S5 from having to reopen this contract.  It is free for every caller:
   create's inum comes from ialloc, whose payout carries exactly this
   bound.

   NOTE ON THE NAME.  [s] is DEFINED as [bname 14 fn], the canonical view of
   the caller's own buffer, so the design's two extra caller obligations
   ("length s <= 14", "nonul s") are NOT premises: they are
   [DirentEnc.bname_length_le] and [DirentEnc.cut_nul_nonul], free.  What
   makes the stored record exactly [de_of_name inum s] is that strncpy's
   post ([SpecStrncpy.snc_post]) forces [bview 14 h = name_pad (bname 14 fn)]
   on both of its arms -- [DirView.snc_bview] is that step.

   THE BUDGET.  writei's [wi_cost off 16] is SEVEN whenever [16 | off]: the
   sixteen bytes never straddle a block, because 1024 = 64*16.  iput wants
   three.  So one constant, [dirlink_units = 7], covers both arms, and the
   postcondition is spend-at-most -- and that is what the COUNTED contract
   takes.

   THE SET-FORM CONTRACT TAKES [dl_need] INSTEAD, and it has to.  Seven is
   not a bound create can meet: its mkdir chain runs its second and third
   [dirlink]s with SIX and FIVE units in hand, so the constant makes the
   whole allocate half unprovable at every path length.  [dl_need crb ind]
   is what the call really wants -- the append arm's [wi16_need] or the
   found arm's [iput_units], whichever is larger -- and it is FOUR wherever
   the append stays inside the directory's direct blocks, which is every
   dirlink create makes on the CHILD.  The two booleans are not new
   parameters: they are [dl16_post]'s own [crb] and [ind], read off the
   entry set and the append slot, so the premise says exactly what the
   postcondition already accounts.                                        *)
```

```coq
(* ProofDirlink.v -- the whole-function proof of dirlink.

     int
     dirlink(struct inode *dp, char *name, uint inum)

   170 bytes.  The shape of the walk, off the decode in CodeDirlink.v:

     +0x00 .. +0x14   the 10-slot frame, FIVE eager saves (ra s0 s2 s5 s6),
                      s0 = sp+80, s2 := dp, s5 := name, s6 := inum
     +0x16            jal dirlookup(dp, name, 0)
     +0x1a            [c.bnez a0]: FOUND -> +0x58
     +0x1c .. +0x22   the LAZY save of s1, s1 := dp->size, [c.beqz s1] -> the
                      empty-directory shortcut at +0x70 (with s1 = 0 = off)
     +0x24 .. +0x2e   the LAZY saves of s3/s4, s1 := 0, s4 := &de, s3 := 16
     +0x30 .. +0x4e   THE FREE-SLOT SCAN: readi, the [lhu] free test (break to
                      +0x6c), off += 16, the size re-read, [bltu] back
     +0x52 .. +0x56   the exhausted exit: restore s3/s4, jump to +0x70
     +0x58 .. +0x5e   THE FOUND ARM: iput(ip), a0 := -1, jump to +0x9c
     +0x60 .. +0x68   panic("dirlink read") -- DEAD
     +0x6c .. +0x6e   the break exit: restore s3/s4
     +0x70 .. +0x8c   strncpy(de.name, name, 14), de.inum := inum, writei
     +0x90 .. +0x96   the BRANCHLESS return: a0 = -(writei(...) != 16)
     +0x9a            the lazy restore of s1
     +0x9c .. +0xa8   the five restores, the pop, [c.ret]

   ---- THE PIECES THE PROOF IS BUILT FROM -------------------------------

   [Htail] -- the epilogue from +0x9c, a [□]-persistent [wp_next]-wrapped
   assertion with an ABSTRACT continuation (ProofDirlookup's shape).  TWO
   arms reach it: the found arm jumps straight to +0x9c (s1 was never saved
   and never clobbered), everything else falls through the [ld s1] at +0x9a.

   [Hafter] -- the shared tail from +0x70, reached by THREE arms (the
   empty-directory shortcut, the scan's break, the scan's exhaustion).  It
   is where strncpy / the [sh] / writei live, so unlike [Htail] it cannot
   hold an abstract continuation: it takes the contract's own continuation,
   spelled out, plus every linear resource writei and the postcondition
   need.

   [Hloop] -- the scan, ProofKexit's [∀ fuel, wp_next] shape (readi sleeps,
   so the hart moves inside the body).  Invariant at +0x30: [i < nrec],
   [dir_free_first data i = None], the register bundle at [off = 16i], and
   the linear resources.  [dir_free_first_step_live] advances it,
   [dir_slot_char] closes both exits at the slot the postcondition names.

   ---- THE FOUR REGISTER BUNDLES ---------------------------------------

   dirlink saves s1/s3/s4 LAZILY and its two early exits skip the matching
   restores, so ONE [callee_saved] transport does not fit the whole
   function.  There are four, each excluding exactly the registers that are
   live-but-unsaved at that point:

     [dl_eregs]  s0 s2 s5 s6 set; s1 s3 s4 still the caller's.  Holds from
                 +0x0e to +0x1e, and on the whole found arm.
     [dl_pregs]  + s1 written (value as a parameter).  +0x1e onwards, and
                 from +0x70 to +0x9a.
     [dl_regs]   + s3 = 16 and s4 = &de.  The scan.
```
